findings.finding: "Skip item" is a first-class PRD action (PRD §11.2 step 4, UI-005 "Skip item") but has NO landing state in the 13-state Item machine. The flow text (USER_FLOWS Flow B: "approve / ... / skip") references it, yet DATA_MODEL's Item state machine only offers `excluded` ("from any state; reversible to needs-review"). Skip and exclude are semantically different: skip = abandon generation early at concept-review without ever producing a mesh/variant; exclude = a generated item kept out of export. Collapsing skip into excluded loses the distinction and creates an item in `excluded` with no variant — which interacts badly with Invariant 1 (exportable requires a selected variant) and with `excluded → reversible to needs-review` (un-excluding a never-generated item lands it in needs-review, an unreachable/incoherent state since it has no preview).
findings.evidence: PRD §11.2 (Workflow B) step 4 lists "skips an item"; PRD §12.5 UI-005 action 6 "Skip item"; USER_FLOWS.md Flow B step lists "skip" as a concept-review action; DATA_MODEL.md Item state machine (lines 45-49) defines only `excluded` and `failed` as off-happy-path states — no `skipped`.
findings.proposedFix: Add an explicit `skipped` item state (entered from concept-review-needed or earlier), distinct from `excluded`, with a defined re-entry transition (skipped → concept-pending on user re-activate). State in the Item machine that an un-excluded never-generated item returns to its pre-generation state, not needs-review.

findings.finding: The PRD §10.3 "Unsupported Generation" workflow (convert-to-nearest-supported WITH USER CONFIRMATION, or mark-unsupported-with-reason) is named in Flow A's system responsibilities but is not represented as (a) an Item lifecycle state and (b) a human review gate. There is no `unsupported` item state, and the "convert with confirmation" is a sixth human-decision point not in the canonical 5-gate list (plan/concept/mesh/overlay/export). An item flagged unsupported during planning has nowhere to live in the 13-state machine — it is neither `planned`, `failed`, nor `excluded`.
findings.evidence: PRD §10.3 (both clauses: convert-with-confirmation; mark-unsupported-with-reason); USER_FLOWS.md Flow A "flag unsupported items (convert-with-confirmation or mark-unsupported)"; DATA_MODEL.md Item machine (lines 45-49) has no `unsupported` state; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §8 / USER_FLOWS gate list enumerates exactly 5 gates with no confirm-conversion gate.
findings.proposedFix: Add an `unsupported` (or `flagged-unsupported`) item state with two exits: convert→`planned` (gated by a user-confirmation decision, which should be added to the gate inventory or explicitly noted as a per-item inline confirmation, not a pipeline interrupt gate) or remain `unsupported` (excluded from generation/export).

findings.finding: ORCH-006 requires the user to "pause, cancel, or skip long-running item generation," and the Run/Step machine has `cancelled`, but the 13-state Item machine has NO cancelled/paused state. When a user cancels an in-flight item (e.g., during mesh-generating), the Run/Step goes `cancelled` but the Item has no defined resting state — it cannot stay in `mesh-generating` (no active run) and the machine offers no `cancelled`/back-to-pending transition for a user-initiated cancel (only `failed` covers system errors, with retry-to-pending). This is a dead/undefined state after a documented user action.
findings.evidence: PRD §16.7 ORCH-006 "must be able to pause, cancel, or skip long-running item generation"; PRD §22.5.3 "Jobs should be cancellable or skippable"; DATA_MODEL.md Run/Step machine (line 51) has `cancelled` but Item machine (lines 45-49) maps only `failed` (system) and `excluded`; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.1 lists `DELETE /jobs/{id}` cooperative cancel but no item-state landing.
findings.proposedFix: Define the item resting state after a user cancel: e.g., on cancel, the item returns to the prior stage's `*-pending` state (or a `cancelled`→`*-pending` transition). If pause is supported per ORCH-006, either add a paused representation or explicitly state pause = run-engine suspend with item staying in `*-generating` (and document that).

findings.finding: The Project state machine cannot reach any failed/cancelled terminal, but Export can end `failed` or `cancelled` (§24.3, ExportArtifact machine). After a failed or cancelled export the Project has no defined state — it ends at `exported` only on success. `validating→curating on blockers` covers validation failure, but a build-stage failure or a user-cancelled export (Flow F "cancelled") leaves the project in `validating`/`exported`-limbo with no transition.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md Project machine (line 42): `created → planned → generating → curating → validating → exported` with only curating⇄generating and validating→curating documented; ExportArtifact machine (line 57) has `failed`/`cancelled`; PRD §24.3 export completion states include "Failed with blockers" and "Cancelled"; USER_FLOWS Flow F lists "failed / cancelled" outcomes.
findings.proposedFix: Add Project transitions for export outcomes: `validating → exporting → {exported | export-failed}` and `exporting → validating` (or `curating`) on cancel/failure, so a failed/cancelled build returns the project to a workable state rather than a dead end.

findings.finding: FunctionalOverlay's `invalid` state is a dead end with no re-entry transition. Flow E only describes retry for "tuning-clone failure" (a generation error), not for the `draft → validated → invalid` compatibility-failure case. PRD §23.4 / FR-FUNC-004 require compatibility validation that can fail; the user must be able to reconfigure and re-validate, but the machine offers no `invalid → draft` (reconfigure) edge.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md FunctionalOverlay machine (line 56): `draft → validated → {approved | invalid}` — `invalid` has no outgoing edge; PRD §23.4 (overlay validation checks), FR-FUNC-004; USER_FLOWS Flow E failure clause covers only "tuning-clone failure → structured error + retry," not validated-but-incompatible.
findings.proposedFix: Add `invalid → draft` (reconfigure-and-revalidate) transition and reflect it in Flow E's failure handling (incompatible source/overlay → return to behavior-configuration step).

findings.finding: AssetVariant — the entity the core export invariant hinges on ("selected AssetVariant") and the immutability invariant protects ("accepted/selected assets are immutable") — has NO state machine, while less load-bearing entities (concept, mesh, overlay, export) each have one. DATA_MODEL claims "6 state machines" but the selected-vs-unselected / accepted lifecycle of AssetVariant is left implicit. "Selected variant" appears in Invariant 1 and the item `export-ready` precondition with no defined transition that sets it, and no state to enforce immutability against.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md lists state machines (lines 41-57) for Project, Item, Run/Step, ConceptCandidate, MeshCandidate, FunctionalOverlay, ExportArtifact — AssetVariant absent; Invariant 1 (line 59) and 4 (immutability) and the Item forbidden-rule "export-ready without a selected variant" all depend on a variant-selection state that is never modeled; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §5 enumerates the same 6 machines.
findings.proposedFix: Add an AssetVariant state machine (e.g., `candidate → selected → accepted/locked`, with `selected → superseded` on re-selection and a confirmation-gated edge out of `locked` per Invariant 4) so the export precondition and immutability invariant have an enforceable state, and reconcile the "6 state machines" count.

findings.finding: Backward "regenerate re-entry" from completed item states is not drawn in the Item machine. UI-006/UI-007 expose "Regenerate concept", "Regenerate mesh", "Rerun cleanup" on items that are already `preview-ready`/`needs-review`/`export-ready`. The machine documents forward forbidden-skips and `failed → that state's pending`, and the Project level notes `curating⇄generating on regenerate`, but the Item-level edges (e.g., `export-ready → mesh-pending` on regenerate-mesh, `preview-ready → concept-pending` on regenerate-concept) are not explicit. Without them, the scoped-repair re-entry (Flow H) is under-specified at the item granularity.
findings.evidence: PRD §12.6 UI-006 actions "Regenerate item / Rerun cleanup"; §12.7 UI-007 "Regenerate concept / Regenerate mesh / Rerun Blender cleanup"; FR-CURATE-003; USER_FLOWS Flow H (scoped repair) describes rerun-only-failed-stage but DATA_MODEL Item machine (lines 45-49) draws no backward edges from completed states into earlier `*-pending` states.
findings.proposedFix: Add explicit re-entry edges to the Item machine for user-initiated regenerate from completed states (preview-ready/needs-review/export-ready → the corresponding earlier `*-pending`), guarded by Invariant 4 (don't overwrite accepted assets without confirmation).

findings.finding: Test-install verification (REQ-O-101, elevated to must-have/anchor) is a Flow F step and a validation gate, but has no lifecycle representation. The Project machine terminates at `exported` with no `installed`/`verified` state and no failure transition for a test-install/path error. USER_FLOWS Flow F even notes "test-install/path error → surfaced, export artifact still retained" — an outcome with no modeled state. For an MVP whose success bar is in-game placeability, the verified-in-game milestone is invisible in the lifecycle.
findings.evidence: PRESEARCH REQ-O-101 ("Test-install ... part of the MVP loop", must-ship anchor); PRD §26.2 vertical-slice AC (in-game checks); USER_FLOWS Flow F "optional test-install ... manual in-game placeability/behavior check" + "test-install/path error → surfaced"; DATA_MODEL Project machine (line 42) ends at `exported`, no install/verify state.
findings.proposedFix: Either add a Project `exported → verified` (or `test-installed`) state plus a `test-install-failed`-but-export-retained transition, or explicitly document that test-install is a side-effect action outside the persisted project lifecycle (and record the verification result on the ExportArtifact).

flows-lifecycle.notes: Audited PRD §6, §10.3, §11 (A-F), §12 (UI-001..011), §16 (ORCH), §20 (entities), §23-24 against USER_FLOWS A-K and the six DATA_MODEL state machines (project / 13-state item / 8-state run-step / concept / mesh / overlay / export). The flow-to-requirement coverage at the FLOW level is genuinely good — the USER_FLOWS coverage table holds up: every FR-* area maps to a flow (A-F + G-K), the 5 human gates are consistent across PRD PIPE-005 / USER_FLOWS / DATA_MODEL invariant 5, and cross-cutting trace/lineage/fail-isolation invariants are wired in. The gaps are at the LIFECYCLE STATE level, not the flow level: several documented user actions (skip, cancel, mark-unsupported, convert-with-confirmation) and several documented failure outcomes (export failed/cancelled, overlay invalid, test-install error) have no resting state or re-entry edge in the state machines, producing unreachable/incoherent or dead states. The most load-bearing items for a human decision before finalizing: (1) skip vs exclude semantics + state, (2) the unsupported-item state + whether convert-with-confirmation is a 6th gate, (3) item-level cancel landing state for ORCH-006, and (4) the missing AssetVariant state machine that the central export/immutability invariants silently depend on. These should be resolved before the binding ARCHITECTURE.md locks the state machines, because /tasks-gen will bind item-status enums and transition guards directly to them.

findings.finding: No structured error taxonomy / error contract is specified anywhere, despite it being named a 'must-handle' production concern. The phrase 'structured errors' / 'actionable message' recurs (ARCH §6.5, §10, USER_FLOWS J, PRESEARCH Phase-8 'error types per stage; creator vs advanced surfacing'), but NO error type set, error codes, error envelope schema, or per-stage error classification is defined. Under production-grade posture this is the spine that makes every other 'surface a structured, actionable error' claim real, and it is the single most-referenced-but-undefined contract.
findings.evidence: PRESEARCH.md:373 lists 'Structured error taxonomy + actionable messages' as classification=must-handle with impact 'error types per stage; creator vs advanced surfacing' — but ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md never defines it. §6.5 only says workers have 'structured errors'; §4A frozen-first contracts list IPC/domain/provider/worker/registry schemas but OMIT an error schema. USER_FLOWS.md:56,80,119 repeatedly promise 'structured error' with no referent. NFR §22.1.5 (PRD) 'Failure messages must be actionable' and FR-3D-006/FR-BLEND-005 require structured errors.
findings.proposedFix: Add an Error Taxonomy section + freeze an ErrorEnvelope as a 6th frozen-first contract in §4A: {code (stable enum: PROVIDER_TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT, PROVIDER_OUTAGE, ARTIFACT_EXPIRED, MESH_QA_FAILED, GEOM_EXPORT_FAILED, DBPF_WRITE_FAILED, BLENDER_CRASH, BLENDER_HANG, TUNING_CLONE_FAILED, TEST_INSTALL_FAILED, VALIDATION_BLOCKER, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, RECONCILE_UNRECOVERABLE...), stage, retryable:bool, creatorMessage, maintainerDetail, suggestedAction, relatedRef, traceRef}. Carry it on Step.error, ValidationResult, IPC SSE error events, and worker contract outputs. Map each code to a recovery action.

findings.finding: Hang / no-progress detection is missing for both subprocess workers and cloud poll loops — only crashes and timeouts are handled. A Blender process that hangs (stuck import, GPU deadlock, infinite remesh) without crashing, or a cloud job stuck in 'processing'/'in_queue' forever (or a provider that drops a job silently), has no watchdog, max-wall-clock, or max-poll-attempts bound. The architecture lists 'timeouts' generically but never defines a hang/deadline policy, so these stages can wedge a run indefinitely.
findings.evidence: RISKS.md:33 trust-boundary names 'crash/hang' for Blender/@s4tk with mitigation only 'process-tree kill; round-trip validation gate' — no hang DETECTION mechanism. ARCH §6.5 says workers have 'timeouts' but §6.4 provider interface is submit/poll/fetch with no max-poll-budget or stuck-job deadline. RESEARCH.md:24 confirms 'Every viable provider is async submit+poll/webhook' yet no poll-attempt ceiling or stale-job giveup is specified. DECISIONS.md ADR-002 notes 'LangGraph has no watchdog' but the app-owned watchdog covers only startup reconcile, not in-run hangs.
findings.proposedFix: Specify per-stage wall-clock deadlines + a watchdog: cloud poll loop gets max-elapsed + max-attempts → emits PROVIDER_TIMEOUT/stuck-job error and transitions Step→failed (retryable); Blender/@s4tk workers get a hard wall-clock timeout independent of crash detection that triggers process-tree kill → BLENDER_HANG. Add a 'stuck job' sweep (job in running > deadline) to the reconciler/job engine, not just to startup.

findings.finding: Test-install failure and the in-game verification loop are happy-path only. The architecture treats test-install as the acceptance bar (CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF:14 'not optional — it's the acceptance bar') but specifies no failure handling for: Sims 4 install not present / wrong Mods path, package copied but the game won't load it, package loads but item won't PLACE, or functional behavior is wrong in-game. The manual in-game check has no defined feedback channel back into project state (no 'in-game verified / failed' status, no ReviewEvent for in-game result, no item state for 'export-built-but-not-placeable').
findings.evidence: USER_FLOWS.md:90,95 only says 'manual in-game placeability/behavior check' and 'test-install/path error → surfaced, export artifact still retained' — silent on the dominant failure (built a package that doesn't actually place, the #1 product risk R1). PRESEARCH.md:229 names the user's core failure as 'content that won't load in-game' yet the 13-state item machine (DATA_MODEL.md:45-49) ends at export-ready with no in-game-verified/in-game-failed state. RISKS.md R1 (Critical/High) is precisely this, and its only test is 'in-game test-install gate' — which has no failure path defined.
findings.proposedFix: Add item/export states for in-game verification (e.g. test-installed, in-game-verified, in-game-failed) and a ReviewEvent type capturing the manual placeability/behavior result. Define test-install preconditions (game-install/Mods-path detection → TEST_INSTALL_FAILED with reason) and the loop on in-game failure (route back to GEOM/DBPF/tuning stage or trigger the R1/R3 fallback). Specify 'structure-only validation' degraded mode when no game install exists (REQ-O-101 / A5 / R16).

findings.finding: GEOM export failure and DBPF write failure are not modeled as distinct, surfaced error+recovery paths in the binding architecture, even though they are the #1 risk. The ExportArtifact state machine has a 'partial' state but there is no defined semantics for partial export at the ITEM granularity (which items succeeded, which failed, what the partial package contains) and no link from a per-item GEOM/DBPF failure to the export-report or to a 'ship loose files' fallback.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md:57 ExportArtifact: building→{success|success-with-warnings|partial|failed|cancelled} — but 'partial' is never defined (which items? is a partial .package valid/installable?). ARCH §6.5/§9 describe the @s4tk worker and clone-a-donor happy path; the only failure mention is the generic round-trip/test-install gate. R1 fallback (RISKS.md:10) 'ship loose files + 1-click S4S project' is a real degraded export mode but is NOT represented as an ExportArtifact buildStatus or export mode. The MESH→GEOM-bytes / PACKAGE split (ADR-005) means a GEOM_EXPORT_FAILED is a different recovery than a DBPF_WRITE_FAILED, but the architecture collapses both.
findings.proposedFix: Define partial-export semantics: per-item export status in ExportReport, what a partial .package contains, and whether it is install-safe. Add 'loose-files / S4S-handoff' as an explicit degraded export mode (buildStatus or exportMode) wired to the R1/R3 fallback. Distinguish GEOM_EXPORT_FAILED (mesh stage) from DBPF_WRITE_FAILED (package stage) with separate scoped-repair entry points per the ADR-005 hard split.

findings.finding: Double-execution / non-idempotent side-effect risk is only partially closed. ADR-002 / R9 correctly wrap cloud calls in @task with job-id-before-side-effect, but the SAME 'node re-runs from top on resume' hazard applies to the local side-effecting workers — Blender writing GEOM/preview files and the @s4tk worker writing a .package / copying into the Mods folder. Re-running these after a crash mid-write can corrupt artifacts, leave half-written .package files, or duplicate Mods-folder installs. No idempotency / atomic-write / write-then-rename contract is specified for the worker outputs or the test-install copy.
findings.evidence: RISKS.md R9 (High/Med) addresses double-BILLED CLOUD jobs only ('@task-wrap external calls; idempotent submit; store job_id before any side effect'). ARCH §6.3 'Cloud steps = two-phase nodes' — local worker steps are NOT described as two-phase/idempotent. §6.5 worker contracts (in/out) and §7 'Accepted assets immutable without confirmation' do not cover crash-mid-write of a NEW artifact or a partially-copied Mods install. RISKS.md trust-boundary 'Export ↔ user's Sims 4 install: never overwrite without confirm' addresses overwrite, not torn writes.
findings.proposedFix: Specify atomic artifact writes (write to temp + fsync + rename) for Blender and @s4tk outputs and an idempotency key per (item,attempt) so re-run after crash overwrites its own in-progress output safely, not an accepted one. Make the test-install copy idempotent (stable target filename, replace-own-prior-install) and transactional (verify copy before marking installed).

findings.finding: Tripo 24h URL expiry is handled for the crash/reconcile path but a happy-path race remains unhandled: a successfully completed cloud 3D job whose result URLs expire BEFORE the fetch step runs (e.g. job completed, app busy/paused, bounded-parallel queue backlog, or the soft-budget pause) — i.e. expiry without a crash. The mitigation everywhere is phrased as 'download promptly' + 'reconcile treats expired-but-succeeded as re-download', which only triggers on reopen/reconcile, not during a long-running but live session.
findings.evidence: ARCH §9:170 '⚠️ Tripo 24h URL expiry → download promptly'. RISKS.md R8 mitigation 'download promptly; persist locally; reconcile treats expired-but-succeeded as re-download' and test 'crash-mid-run → resume test' — all crash-framed. RESEARCH.md:25 'reconcile treats expired-but-succeeded as needs-redownload'. None covers a live session where fetch is deferred past 24h (paused run, queue backpressure under R5, or budget-warning pause at USER_FLOWS B/J).
findings.proposedFix: Define an ARTIFACT_EXPIRED error code + a fetch-deadline check: persist completed-job artifacts immediately on poll-success regardless of pipeline pacing; if a URL is found expired at fetch time and the artifact was never persisted, surface ARTIFACT_EXPIRED with recovery = re-submit (re-bill) with explicit user/cost acknowledgment. Make 'download promptly' a concrete invariant (fetch in the same node as poll-success, not a downstream stage).

findings.finding: LangSmith fail-open is asserted but its failure boundary is under-specified, and trace-loss is not surfaced. 'Fail-open' (a LangSmith outage never blocks a run) is repeated, but there is no spec for: bounded trace-emit timeout/buffering so a slow/hanging LangSmith endpoint doesn't stall stages, what happens to the OBS-001 'every run must create a trace' guarantee when traces are dropped, or how the maintainer learns traces were lost for a run. Fail-open without a local fallback record means observability silently degrades exactly when something is going wrong.
findings.evidence: ARCH §1/§7/§9/§15 + ADR-007 + REQ-O-102 all say 'fail-open' but only at the level 'must never block or fail a generation run'. PRD OBS-001 §18.1 mandates 'Every pipeline run must create a trace or trace-equivalent record' — a hard requirement that fail-open silently violates with no fallback. ADR-007 caveat covers data-egress + offline but not emit-timeout/back-pressure or trace-loss visibility. DATA_MODEL.md invariant 9 'Every state-changing action emits a Trace' becomes unenforceable if the only trace sink is a dropped remote call.
findings.proposedFix: Specify: trace emission is async + bounded-timeout (never blocks a stage even when LangSmith hangs, not just when it's down); a minimal local trace/step record (already in Postgres per §7) is the durable trace-of-record so OBS-001 holds offline; emit a maintainer-visible signal (dev-panel badge / log) when remote tracing is degraded so trace-loss isn't silent. This makes 'fail-open' satisfy OBS-001 rather than override it.

findings.finding: Cooperative cancel of an in-flight cloud job is under-specified — cancellation of long jobs is promised but its cloud-side semantics are missing. DELETE /jobs/{id} cancels the local step, but whether the remote provider job is cancelled (to stop cost) or merely abandoned (still billed, still occupying queue) is undefined, as is what happens to a result that arrives after cancel.
findings.evidence: ARCH §6.1 'DELETE /jobs/{id} (or WS) for cooperative cancel'; PRD ORCH-006 §16.7 'user must be able to pause, cancel, or skip long-running item generation'; Run/Step machine has a 'cancelled' state (DATA_MODEL.md:51). No provider-interface cancel method exists (§6.4 is submit/poll/fetch only) and R5 cost-control doesn't mention cancel stopping spend.
findings.proposedFix: Add an optional cancel(job_id) to the provider interface (best-effort, since not all providers support it) and define post-cancel behavior: mark Step cancelled, stop polling, and if a result still arrives, persist-or-discard deterministically. Note cost implication (abandoned remote job may still bill) in the soft-budget surface.

findings.finding: Mid-run crash recovery is well-designed for reconcilable cloud jobs but the UNRECONCILABLE case is thin: providers without poll-by-id (or webhook-only providers after a missed webhook) leave a job whose status can't be re-derived on reopen. USER_FLOWS I says 'where the provider supports it' and 'mark unrecoverable steps for retry', but retry of a non-idempotent paid generation = silent re-bill, and there's no user-facing 'this in-flight job is unknown, re-run (will re-charge) or abandon?' decision point.
findings.evidence: USER_FLOWS.md:114-116 'reconcile in-flight cloud jobs by re-polling provider job IDs WHERE THE PROVIDER SUPPORTS IT … mark unrecoverable steps for retry'. ARCH §6.2 reconciler 're-polls in-flight cloud jobs by stored provider+job_id' — assumes poll-by-id exists. No defined UX/state for 'job_id unresolvable'. RESEARCH.md:24 notes webhook-where-available; a missed webhook with no poll fallback is unhandled.
findings.proposedFix: Define a RECONCILE_UNRECOVERABLE outcome with an explicit user decision (re-run with cost acknowledgment vs abandon vs treat-as-failed), rather than auto-retrying a paid step. Require poll-by-id as a provider-interface capability flag; webhook-only providers must declare a poll fallback or be marked non-reconcilable up front.

failure-modes.notes:
Posture = production-grade; judged accordingly. The planning set is unusually strong on failure modes at the RISK-REGISTER level — RISKS.md (R1-R16 + trust-boundary table) and USER_FLOWS.md (System Flows H/I/J) name almost every failure I went hunting for: provider outage/timeout/rate-limit (R5/Flow J), Tripo 24h expiry (R8), Blender crash (R3/Flow C/J), resume double-billing (R9), orphan processes/ports (R10), secrets leak (R11), LangSmith offline (R6/REQ-O-102), EA patch drift (R7), no-game-install (R16). That breadth is real and credited — this dimension is NOT empty, but it is also far from a happy-path-only draft.

The adversarial gaps concentrate in ONE place that matters most: the document that becomes the binding contract, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md, defers essentially all error-path SPECIFICS to companion-doc prose pointers and names no concrete error contract. Three findings are critical+load-bearing and need a human decision before finalize: (1) there is no error taxonomy / ErrorEnvelope anywhere despite it being tagged must-handle — every 'surface a structured, actionable error' promise currently dangles; (2) HANG/no-progress detection is absent for both subprocess workers and cloud poll loops (only crash+generic-timeout exist) so a stuck Blender or a forever-'processing' cloud job can wedge a run; (3) the test-install / in-game verification loop — explicitly THE acceptance bar and the #1 product risk (R1) — is happy-path only, with no item/export state for 'built but won't place', no feedback channel from the manual in-game check, and no degraded path when no game install exists.

The four important findings are gaps where a named risk is only half-closed in the binding doc: partial/per-item EXPORT failure + the loose-files fallback isn't modeled as a real export mode; the idempotency/atomic-write guarantee that R9 gives CLOUD calls is NOT extended to LOCAL side-effecting workers (Blender file writes, @s4tk .package writes, Mods-folder copy) so a crash mid-write can tear artifacts; Tripo expiry is closed for crash/reconcile but a live-session deferred-fetch expiry race remains; and LangSmith 'fail-open' lacks an emit-timeout + local trace-of-record so it silently violates OBS-001's 'every run must create a trace'.

Recommended sequencing for the finalizer: freeze an ErrorEnvelope as the 6th frozen-first contract in §4A and add an Error Taxonomy + recovery-action table to §6/§15 BEFORE tracks fan out, since every worker/provider/IPC contract output depends on it. The hang-detection and idempotent-local-write specs should land in §6.5 (workers) and §6.2/§6.3 (engine/graph). The in-game-verification state machine extension belongs in §5/DATA_MODEL and is load-bearing because spike S1 (R1) is the gating unknown and currently has no failure path defined.

findings.finding: No error schema / structured-error taxonomy is defined for ANY of the five frozen-first contracts (IPC, provider, worker, registry, domain). The architecture repeatedly *promises* 'structured errors' (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.5 'structured errors'; USER_FLOWS Flow C 'structured failure'; PRESEARCH Phase-8 'Structured error taxonomy + actionable messages — must-handle') and the PRD mandates creator-vs-advanced error surfacing (NFR §22.1.5 'failure messages must be actionable', FR-3D-006, FR-BLEND-005), but no error object is specified: no error code enum, no {code, message, retryable, userFacingMessage, advancedDetail, stage, cause} shape, no mapping of provider/Blender/@s4tk failures to a common envelope. Under production-grade posture, an unspecified error contract means every track (UI mocks, sidecar, workers, adapters) will invent incompatible error shapes, and PIPE-002's requirement that 'mock adapters produce realistic ... failure states' is unbuildable because there is no failure shape to mock.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4A lists the 5 frozen-first contracts but none includes an error schema; §6.5 says 'structured errors' without defining one. PRESEARCH Phase-8 table row 'Structured error taxonomy ... must-handle ... error types per stage'. PRD FR-3D-006 / FR-BLEND-005 / §22.1.5. DATA_MODEL Step has 'error?' field with no type; ValidationResult has severity enum but is NOT the runtime error type.
findings.proposedFix: Add a Section-6 error-contract subsection (or a 6th frozen contract) defining a single ErrorEnvelope {code (stable enum, namespaced per stage/provider), category (validation|provider|worker|timeout|cost|internal), retryable: bool, userMessage, detail, stage, runId?, stepId?, cause?} shared py↔ts, plus the enumerated code set per stage. Bind every adapter/worker/IPC failure path to it; make mock adapters emit it.

findings.finding: The IPC REST contract is named but never specified: no endpoint list with methods/paths, no request/response bodies, no status-code semantics, no SSE event-type catalog or per-event payload schema, no cancel semantics beyond 'DELETE /jobs/{id} (or WS)'. §6.1 enumerates *commands* in prose ('create project, start run, approve gate, include/exclude, edit, export, test-install, rerun-step') but does not bind them to routes or schemas. The five PRD human-review gates (PIPE-005) need a precise 'approve gate' payload (which gate, which run/item, decision, optional edits) tied to LangGraph's interrupt()/Command(resume) — that resume-payload shape is undefined. This is the system spine (§4A 'frozen first') and is not freezable as written.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.1 prose-only command list; §4A item 1 'IPC contract (REST command schema + SSE event schema + cancel)' declared frozen-first but no schema present. REQ-I-101 'versioned, mockable boundary'. RESEARCH line 60 'IPC contract: REST commands + SSE progress/logs + DELETE/WS cancel'. PRD PIPE-005 five gates; ADR-002 interrupt()/Command(resume).
findings.proposedFix: Add an IPC contract table: each command → METHOD path, request schema, success response, error codes, and the SSE event taxonomy (event types: progress, step-state, log, validation, cost, gate-needed, done, error) each with a typed payload. Define the gate-resume payload {runId, gate, itemId?, decision: approve|reject|regenerate|skip, edits?} and the cancel response/idempotency. Pin SSE resumability (Last-Event-ID semantics: what id, what replay window).

findings.finding: py↔ts type-sync mechanism is asserted but undecided, leaving the single most load-bearing contract guarantee unbuildable as a guarantee. §13 says domain types are 'generated OR hand-synced to TS' — that 'or' is the gap: hand-sync silently drifts (a known production failure mode), and no generator (e.g. pydantic→JSON-Schema→ts, datamodel-code-generator, openapi-typescript) is chosen, nor a CI drift check. §4A demands the shared contracts package be 'frozen first' and imported by 'everyone', but Python (pydantic) and TS (UI + Node @s4tk worker) cannot share a frozen contract without a concrete, verified sync path. The Node @s4tk worker also consumes domain/worker types, so this is a THREE-language sync problem (py sidecar, ts UI, node worker), not two.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §13 'domain types/schemas as the single source of truth, generated or hand-synced to TS'; §4A 'pydantic (Python) ↔ TS types (UI/Node), kept in sync' with no mechanism. Repo has empty packages/ (no contracts package exists). CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF lists 'domain types' as a frozen-first contract Brain 2 must pin.
findings.proposedFix: Pick ONE source of truth (pydantic models) and ONE generation path to TS (e.g. pydantic → JSON Schema → openapi-typescript / json-schema-to-typescript), emit the Node worker's types from the same schema, and add a CI gate that fails on drift (regenerate-and-diff). Document the command and where generated artifacts live in packages/contracts/.

findings.finding: No contract is versioned despite 'versioned' being claimed. §6.1 and REQ-I-101 say the IPC contract is 'versioned + mockable', and §4A calls all five contracts 'frozen first', but there is no version field defined anywhere (no contractVersion on the IPC envelope, no schemaVersion on domain entities, no registry-schema version, no on-disk project schema_version). PRESEARCH Phase-8 explicitly flags 'Local store schema versioning + migration' and REQ-D-101 requires 'older project opens after schema bump' — but the domain entities in DATA_MODEL carry no version field, so migration has nothing to dispatch on. For a local-first app with long-lived projects + an evolving cloud-provider surface, unversioned contracts are a production-grade gap.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.1 'Contract is versioned'; §4A 'frozen-first'; REQ-I-101 + REQ-D-101 (PRESEARCH Phase-6) require schema versioning/migration; DATA_MODEL entity table has NO version/schemaVersion field on Project/ItemSpec/etc. (CollectionPlan has a domain 'version' but that is plan-iteration, not schema-version). PRESEARCH Phase-8 'Local store schema versioning + migration ... versioned project schema + migration path'.
findings.proposedFix: Define an explicit version surface: IPC contractVersion (negotiated at connect/health), domain schemaVersion on persisted entities, registry-file schemaVersion, and the Alembic migration ↔ schemaVersion relationship. State the back/forward-compat policy (reject vs migrate vs warn) for UI↔sidecar version skew.

findings.finding: Provider interface signatures are inconsistent across docs and missing fields needed for the locked reconcile-resume spine. §6.4 specifies submit(input,params)→job_id · poll(job_id)→{status,progress,urls} · fetch(urls)→artifacts, but: (a) the poll status value-set is never enumerated (queued|running|succeeded|failed? maps to which Step state?); (b) there is no provider/model identity carried on job_id, yet §6.2's reconciler must 're-poll by stored provider+job_id' — the interface returns a bare job_id with no provider tag; (c) RESEARCH line 25 shows submit(image,params) for Image3D while §6.4 shows submit(input,params) generically and ImageGen/LLM signatures are never given their own shapes (LLM is not submit/poll/fetch-shaped — it's structured-output, but §4A lumps it under the same submit/poll/fetch bullet); (d) cost metadata is required ('cost per op', OBS-001 field 13) but no field on the poll/fetch result carries it; (e) Tripo 24h-URL expiry (R8) needs an artifact-persisted-locally flag the fetch contract doesn't define.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.4 (submit/poll/fetch) vs RESEARCH line 25 submit(image,params) vs §4A line 99 'submit/poll/fetch' applied to all three including LLMProvider. ADR-014 LLMProvider is structured-output (planner/judge), not async-job-shaped. §6.2 'stored provider+job_id'. OBS-001 field 13 cost/latency; R8 Tripo URL expiry. DATA_MODEL MeshCandidate has adapter/adapterConfig but no provider-job-id field.
findings.proposedFix: Specify three distinct interfaces: Image3DProvider & ImageGenProvider as submit/poll/fetch with an enumerated PollStatus, a ProviderJobRef {provider, model, jobId, submittedAt, expiresAt?} persisted in state, and cost/latency on results; LLMProvider as a separate synchronous structured-output interface (complete(messages, schema)→validated object + usage/cost). Add the artifact-persistence flag to fetch results for expiry reconcile.

findings.finding: Worker contracts (BlenderJob, ExportJob) are described only as in/out prose with no field-level schema, no idempotency/run-correlation keys, and no result-report schema. §4A defines BlenderJob '(in: mesh/params; out: cleaned GEOM/preview/report)' and ExportJob '(in: donor + GEOM + textures + tuning edits + TGI keys; out: .package + report)' — but 'params', 'report', 'tuning edits', and 'TGI keys' are undefined types. The Blender 'report' must carry the game-ready-gate results (LOD count, per-tile poly budget pass, normal/UV validation, bbox) that EVAL-004/005 and Mesh Validation (§23.2) assert against — that schema is the contract those evals bind to and it does not exist. ExportJob crosses a process boundary (Node @s4tk) so its in/out must be a serializable contract (JSON + file paths), which is unspecified.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4A item 4 (BlenderJob/ExportJob in/out prose); §6.5 'worker contracts §4A'; PRD §23.2 Mesh Validation checks + EVAL-004/005 pass criteria (orientation/scale/origin/normals/LOD/poly budget) — these need a typed Blender report. ADR-005 ExportJob fields 'OBJD-tuning/FTPT/RIG/SLOT ... TGI keys' named but untyped. DATA_MODEL 'Ambiguous Terms: exact required DBPF resource set per archetype — research required'.
findings.proposedFix: Define BlenderJobInput/BlenderJobReport and ExportJobInput/ExportJobReport as explicit serializable schemas (the worker IPC envelope: JSON over stdin/stdout or a job file + result file). BlenderReport must enumerate the game-ready-gate metrics; ExportReport the written resource TGIs + validation. Flag the DBPF-resource-set fields as spike-S1-pending but stub the contract shape now.

findings.finding: Registry schemas (PlacementType, FunctionalArchetype, DonorMapping) are the load-bearing 'open registries' (ADR-010) but their field types and validation rules are named, not specified — and the rule fields are free-form. DATA_MODEL gives FunctionalArchetype {tuningGraftRules, eligibilityRules, validationRules} and DonorMapping {donorObjectKey, requiredResources[], tuningKeys[], preserveKeys[]} but never defines what a 'tuningGraftRule' or 'eligibilityRule' IS (DSL? predicate? data shape?). The whole extensibility claim — 'adding an archetype = registry entry + donor + test, no engine rewrite' (ADR-010, REQ-F-102/106) — is only true if the rule schema is expressive-yet-typed; an unspecified rule grammar means the generic overlay engine cannot be built against it and new entries will require engine changes (defeating the ADR). Also no registry-entry validation contract or load-time schema check is specified despite Invariant 6 ('only registered ... are assignable, validated').
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL FunctionalArchetype/DonorMapping/PlacementType key-fields rows (rules named, untyped); Invariant 6 'open registries, validated — not fixed enums'; ADR-010 'adding a functional archetype = registry entry + donor + test (no engine rewrite)'; REQ-F-102/106. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.6 'data-driven ... with validation' (no schema). RISKS R2 (tuning-clone breadth) is the spike that should produce this schema.
findings.proposedFix: Specify the registry-entry JSON schemas including the rule sub-grammars (eligibility predicate shape, tuning-graft operation list, validation-rule list) and a load-time validator. Tie the schema to spike S3's output (one archetype proves the rule shape) and state that the rule grammar — not engine code — is what new archetypes extend.

findings.finding: LangGraph typed State is named the integration carrier ('typed State carries artifacts + provider job_ids + status', §6.3) but is never reconciled with the domain/IPC schemas — it is effectively a 6th undefined contract. The State shape determines what the SSE stream can project (step-state/progress events derive from it), what the reconciler enumerates, and what checkpoints persist; it must agree field-for-field with the DATA_MODEL Step/PipelineRun entities and the IPC event payloads. No mapping State↔domain↔IPC is given, so the three could diverge.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.3 'typed State carries artifacts + provider job_ids + status'; ADR-002 'typed State carries artifacts + provider job_ids + status; one thread_id per run'; DATA_MODEL PipelineRun/Step entities. No State schema or State↔domain mapping anywhere.
findings.proposedFix: Define the LangGraph State TypedDict/pydantic schema and an explicit mapping table State field → persisted Step/PipelineRun field → SSE event field, so checkpoint, store, and stream stay consistent. Note which State fields are projected to the UI vs internal-only.

findings.finding: Idempotency is required at the run/command layer but no idempotency-key field is defined on the IPC command contract. R9 (resume double-execution / double-billing) is mitigated at the graph layer (@task + job_id-before-side-effect), but the UI↔sidecar command layer also needs idempotency (RISKS trust-boundary row says 'idempotent commands') — e.g. a retried 'start run' or 'build export' after an SSE disconnect should not launch a duplicate. No requestId/idempotencyKey is specified on commands.
findings.evidence: RISKS trust-boundary table, UI↔Sidecar row: 'idempotent commands; reconnect+replay'. RISKS R9 (double-execution). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.1 command list has no idempotency field. USER_FLOWS Flow I reconnect-resume.
findings.proposedFix: Add an optional idempotencyKey/requestId to mutating IPC commands and define server-side dedup behavior (return the in-flight/just-completed result instead of re-executing), especially for start-run / build-export / approve-gate after reconnect.

interfaces-schemas.notes:
Scope: this is a planning-stage audit — the repo has only PRD.md + docs/planning/ + empty packages/services dirs (no code, no contracts package yet), so all findings are against the draft + planning artifacts, judged under the production-grade posture per CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF.

The draft is internally self-aware that these five contracts must be 'frozen first' (§4A) and even tells Brain 2 to 'pin these in ARCHITECTURE.md §6/§4a before tracks fan out' (CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF). My finding is that the draft NAMES all five contracts but specifies NONE of them to a buildable, freezable level — they are prose declarations, not schemas. That is precisely the dimension-4 failure mode (underspecified interfaces). This is not over-build; the contract coverage map is right, the depth is missing.

The four critical findings cluster on production-grade non-negotiables that are explicitly promised yet absent: (1) no error schema, (2) no concrete IPC REST+SSE+cancel schema/event catalog, (3) py↔ts (actually py↔ts↔node, three languages) sync is an undecided 'generated or hand-synced' with no drift gate, (4) no version field anywhere despite 'versioned'/'frozen' claims and a REQ-D-101 migration requirement that has no schemaVersion to dispatch on.

Load-bearing items needing a human decision before finalize: the type-sync mechanism (generate vs hand-sync — pick one + CI gate); the LLMProvider interface shape (it is wrongly lumped with submit/poll/fetch and is actually synchronous structured-output); and the registry rule-grammar, which is genuinely coupled to spike S3 and may be partly deferred-but-stubbed. Several gaps (Blender report schema, DBPF resource set, registry rules) legitimately depend on spikes S1/S3 — the fix is to stub the contract SHAPE now and fill fields post-spike, not to leave them entirely unnamed.

Recommend Brain 2 add to ARCHITECTURE.md §6: (a) an ErrorEnvelope + per-stage code enum, (b) a full IPC endpoint+SSE-event+gate-resume+cancel table, (c) a concrete type-sync pipeline + CI drift gate, (d) an explicit version surface (contractVersion/schemaVersion/registry version) with a skew/migration policy, (e) typed Provider/Worker/Registry/State schemas with spike-gated fields marked. These are the actual frozen-first deliverables the draft defers.

findings.finding: DATA_MODEL.md and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT/DECISIONS/PRESEARCH name DIFFERENT primary sources of truth for the SAME state. DATA_MODEL.md (the canonical domain artifact) says — in its header (line 6), in every 'Source of Truth' column entry (Project/CollectionPlan/PipelineRun/ExportArtifact = 'local store', lines 13-28), and in its Data Authority section (line 86, 'Authoritative (persisted, local)') — that the source of truth is the 'local project store (per-project folder on disk; a project DB/JSON index + artifact files).' But ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §7 (line 154), DECISIONS ADR-009 (line 111), and PRESEARCH REQ-D-101 (line 313) say the source of truth is an app-managed Postgres DB + filesystem artifacts. 'DB/JSON index' and 'per-project folder' are not Postgres. A coding agent reading DATA_MODEL (the doc that literally owns the source-of-truth column) would build per-project on-disk JSON/SQLite stores; one reading the architecture would build one shared Postgres. This is the single most load-bearing ambiguity in the whole package and it is internally contradictory across the binding inputs.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md line 6 ('Source of truth = the local project store ... a project DB/JSON index + artifact files'), lines 13/14/25/28 ('Source of Truth' column = 'local store'), line 86 ('Authoritative (persisted, local): Project, CollectionPlan ...'); vs ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 154 ('Source of truth = app-managed Postgres'), DECISIONS.md ADR-009 line 111, PRESEARCH.md REQ-D-101 line 313.
findings.proposedFix: Pick ONE in ARCHITECTURE.md §7 and make it binding: app-managed Postgres = single relational/state source of truth; filesystem = artifact bytes only (referenced by path). Then rewrite DATA_MODEL.md's header line 6 and the entire 'Source of Truth' column to say 'Postgres' (state rows) vs 'filesystem' (artifact bytes) explicitly per entity, and delete the 'project DB/JSON index' / 'per-project folder = source of truth' language so no agent builds a second store.

findings.finding: Trace ownership is double-claimed and contradictory. DATA_MODEL.md lists Trace and ReviewEvent as 'Append-only authoritative' persisted LOCALLY (line 30 'Source of Truth = append-only', line 87 'Append-only authoritative: Trace, ReviewEvent'). But ADR-007 (line 84) and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §1/§7 send traces to LangSmith SaaS, with the explicit constraint that tracing is FAIL-OPEN (a LangSmith outage must never block a run, REQ-O-102). If LangSmith is fail-open it CANNOT be the authoritative store for trace data (data is dropped on outage); but if the local DB is authoritative for traces, then the architecture never says the sidecar persists traces locally — it only describes emitting LangSmith spans. ReviewEvent has the same split: DATA_MODEL says authoritative-local, ADR-007 line 84 says 'Capture user accept/reject as LangSmith feedback/runs', and OBS-004/EVAL-009 require this preference data be durable product data. Fail-open + sole-store-is-SaaS = silent loss of OBS-001/OBS-004 data, which the PRD mandates (OBS-001 'Every pipeline run must create a trace'; OBS-004 review events 'must be captured as product data').
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md line 30 (Trace 'Source of Truth = append-only'), line 87; PRD §18 OBS-001 (line 988) + OBS-004 (line 1036); ADR-007 line 84 (LangSmith feedback/runs) + fail-open; PRESEARCH REQ-O-102 line 315 ('a LangSmith outage/offline must never block or fail a generation run'). No artifact states the sidecar writes Trace/ReviewEvent rows to Postgres.
findings.proposedFix: Declare in ARCHITECTURE.md that Postgres is the authoritative store for Trace summaries and ReviewEvent/preference rows (satisfies OBS-001/OBS-004/EVAL-009 durably); LangSmith is a DERIVED, fail-open mirror for the dev/observability UX only. Add an explicit 'write to Postgres first, then emit to LangSmith (best-effort)' ordering so fail-open never drops mandated product data, and fix DATA_MODEL.md to say Trace/ReviewEvent source-of-truth = Postgres (append-only), LangSmith = derived mirror.

findings.finding: The 'sidecar is sole writer' claim is asserted but not sound: two distinct writers touch the SAME Postgres database with no ownership partition. ADR-002 (line 41) puts the LangGraph PostgresSaver checkpointer in the SAME DB as the app repository layer (ADR-009 line 111: 'LangGraph PostgresSaver shares the same DB'). So pipeline state exists in TWO representations — the LangGraph checkpoint (graph State carries 'artifacts + provider job_ids + status', §6.3 line 133) AND the app's domain rows (PipelineRun/Step/candidates). Both are written during a run. The draft never says which is authoritative when they disagree, nor how the app repo's Step state (§6.2) stays consistent with the checkpoint's status. On reconcile (§6.2 line 130 'enumerate incomplete threads'), the reconciler reads checkpoint state but must reconcile it against domain rows the checkpointer didn't write. The 'single-writer lock' (ADR-002) only prevents two PROCESSES resuming the same thread; it does nothing about the two LOGICAL writers (checkpointer vs repo) inside one process writing overlapping state.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md ADR-002 line 41 ('app owns the startup reconciler + a single-writer lock; LangGraph has no watchdog/dup-prevention'); ADR-009 line 111 ('LangGraph PostgresSaver shares the same DB'); ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.2 line 128-130 (job engine persists run/step state) vs §6.3 line 132-134 (typed State carries artifacts/job_ids/status); RISKS.md trust-boundary row 'UI ↔ Sidecar' ('sidecar = sole writer').
findings.proposedFix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2/§6.3, define ownership explicitly: the LangGraph checkpoint is authoritative for in-flight graph execution position ONLY (resume mechanics); the app repository (PipelineRun/Step/candidate/variant rows) is authoritative for durable product state and is the ONLY thing UI/queries read. State the projection direction (graph node -> repo write, never the reverse) and the rule that domain rows are written transactionally by stage-completion handlers, not derived from checkpoints. Clarify the single-writer lock is per-thread-resume, and name the in-process invariant that only the repo layer writes domain tables.

findings.finding: No ownership/reconciliation rule between the two physical stores (Postgres path-refs vs filesystem artifact bytes). Postgres holds path references; bytes live on disk (§4 line 86-87, §7, ADR-009 line 111). Multiple writers create files: the Blender worker writes GEOM/preview/normalized-intermediate, the @s4tk worker writes .package, provider adapters fetch() downloads to disk (§6.4 line 137 'fetch(urls)->local artifacts'), the image-gen adapter writes concept images. The DB row that references each file is written by the sidecar repo. Nothing states the ordering (write file then row? row then file?), what happens to orphaned files when a row write fails or a run is cancelled mid-fetch, or what happens to dangling DB refs if a file is deleted/never written. R8 (provider artifact expiry) and 'accepted assets immutable' (invariant 4) both depend on this file<->row consistency but it is never specified. Artifact GC is explicitly deferred (§18), which makes orphan accumulation a known unmanaged surface.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §4 line 86-88, §6.4 line 137 ('fetch(urls)->local artifacts'), §6.5 (Blender/export workers write files); DATA_MODEL.md invariant 4 (line 66) + entity 'Source of Truth' rows pointing to file paths; RISKS.md R8 (artifact expiry); §18 line 234 (artifact GC deferred).
findings.proposedFix: Add an 'artifact store contract' subsection to ARCHITECTURE.md §7: define the canonical on-disk layout, a write-bytes-then-commit-row ordering (so a crash leaves an orphan file, never a dangling ref), who owns each artifact subtree (workers write into sidecar-owned paths only — workers never write DB rows), and a reconcile-on-startup sweep that detects orphan files and dangling refs even though active GC is deferred.

findings.finding: Worker-output ownership is ambiguous: the draft says workers run as subprocesses behind contracts but does not pin that workers NEVER write Postgres or the canonical artifact tree directly — only the sidecar does. §6.5/§4A describe BlenderJob/ExportJob contracts as (in: params; out: GEOM/preview/report or .package/report), which reads as 'worker returns bytes/paths to the sidecar.' But §4 line 80-81 and §9 line 173-174 say the @s4tk worker 'reads donor .package from the user's game install' and 'writes DBPF', and the Blender worker writes preview/normalized-intermediate files — i.e. workers are doing filesystem writes. If workers write into the project artifact tree directly, they are second writers to the filesystem store; if they write to a scratch dir and hand bytes back, the sidecar is sole writer. This is exactly the 'state written by two processes (Python/Node/Blender)' question and it is left implicit.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §4A line 100-102 (worker contracts 'out: cleaned GEOM/preview/report' / 'out: .package + report'), §4 line 80-81, §9 line 173-174 ('@s4tk ... writes DBPF'; Blender writes preview/intermediate); §15 trust boundary (d) 'validate inputs/outputs ... before state writes'.
findings.proposedFix: State the rule in §6.5: workers write only to a sidecar-provided scratch/output directory and return paths; the SIDECAR (repo layer) is the only writer of the canonical artifact tree AND of all Postgres rows after it validates worker output (§15 boundary d). This makes 'sidecar = sole writer' literally true for both stores and resolves the Python/Node/Blender multi-writer question.

findings.finding: Entity count and naming drift between artifacts undermines a single authoritative domain model. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §5 line 115 says '16 entities, 6 state machines, 10 invariants'; PRESEARCH §5 line 283 also says '16 entities ... 6 state machines'; but DATA_MODEL.md's Core Entities table lists more than 16 rows and folds StyleBible/Swatch/registries in inconsistently, and the PRD §20 enumerates only 11 product entities. More importantly the 'Source of Truth' assignments in DATA_MODEL are internally inconsistent with the relational model the architecture mandates: e.g. StyleBible source-of-truth = 'CollectionPlan', Swatch = 'AssetVariant', DonorMapping = 'registry (data-driven)'. Mixing 'owning parent entity' and 'physical store' in one column means there is no single answer to 'where does this state live' for half the entities once the store is Postgres.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §5 line 115 ('16 entities'); PRESEARCH.md line 283 ('16 entities'); DATA_MODEL.md Core Entities table lines 13-32 (Source of Truth column mixes 'local store', parent-entity names like 'CollectionPlan'/'AssetVariant'/'ItemSpec', and 'registry (data-driven)'); PRD §20 (11 entities).
findings.proposedFix: In ARCHITECTURE.md/DATA_MODEL split the conflated column into two: (a) Owning entity (FK parent) and (b) Physical store (Postgres table vs filesystem vs registry file). Reconcile the entity count to one number across §5, PRESEARCH §5, and DATA_MODEL, and note the mapping to the PRD's 11 product entities so nothing is silently added/dropped.

findings.finding: Registry source-of-truth is unstated: are PlacementType/FunctionalArchetype/DonorMapping authoritative in Postgres rows, or in version-controlled config files on disk? DATA_MODEL marks them 'registry (data-driven)' (lines 22-24); ADR-010/§6.6 call them 'data-driven, validated registries' where 'adding an entry is config'; §13 (Shared/config) lists 'donor registry' under Config alongside feature flags and paths. 'Config' implies a file in the repo/app bundle (version-controlled, shipped); 'app-managed Postgres holds registries' (§7 line 154 explicitly lists registries in Postgres) implies DB rows (user-editable at runtime, in the local DB). These are mutually exclusive sources of truth with very different implications for: editing a donor mapping at runtime, shipping registry updates to existing installs, and migration. R7 (EA patch drift -> re-validate/re-pin donors) cannot be planned without knowing whether donors live in shipped config or per-install DB rows.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md lines 22-24 ('registry (data-driven)'); DECISIONS.md ADR-010 line 118 ('adding a placement type = config'); ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §7 line 154 (Postgres holds 'registries'), §13 line 196-197 (Config includes 'donor registry'), §6.6 line 144-145; RISKS.md R7.
findings.proposedFix: Decide and state in ARCHITECTURE.md §6.6/§13: registries ship as version-controlled config files = source of truth (auditable, updatable across installs), loaded/validated into Postgres at startup as a read cache/index; OR Postgres rows are authoritative and seeded-then-user-editable. Either way name the single authority and the seed/migration path, and reconcile the §7 'Postgres holds registries' line with the §13 'Config' classification.

findings.finding: Derived/recomputable state is well-bounded but the boundary with authoritative state is not enforced anywhere in the contract. DATA_MODEL line 89-90 cleanly lists status badges, cost/latency estimates, validation rollups, thumbnails, preview composites as 'Derived/display (recomputable), never the source of truth.' Good. But ValidationResult is marked 'derived per run' (line 27) while invariant 1 and FR-VAL-004 make export-blocking decisions FROM validation results — i.e. a derived artifact is load-bearing for a hard gate. If validation results are purely recomputable and not persisted authoritatively, the export gate's auditability (export report must include 'validation summary', PRD §24.2) depends on transient data.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md line 27 (ValidationResult 'derived per run'), line 89-90 (derived/display list), invariant 1 line 60-61; PRD FR-VAL-004 (line 1439) + §24.2 export report 'Validation summary' (line 1595).
findings.proposedFix: Clarify in ARCHITECTURE.md that ValidationResults used for the export gate are persisted (authoritative snapshot at export time) so the export report and gate decision are reproducible/auditable, distinct from transient validation re-runs in the UI; keep purely cosmetic rollups (badges/thumbnails) as the recomputable class.

source-of-truth.notes: Posture applied: production-grade (durability, idempotency, single-writer, observability treated as critical). This dimension is NOT clean — it contains the package's most load-bearing internal contradiction. Net: the source-of-truth story is asserted confidently ("sidecar is sole writer," "source of truth = Postgres") but is not actually unambiguous when traced across artifacts. Two critical, must-resolve-before-finalize items: (1) DATA_MODEL.md says the source of truth is a per-project on-disk "DB/JSON index + folder" while ARCHITECTURE/DECISIONS/PRESEARCH say app-managed Postgres — a direct contradiction in the binding inputs that would split a coding agent's data layer in two; (2) Trace/ReviewEvent are claimed both as locally-authoritative-append-only (DATA_MODEL) and as LangSmith SaaS records (ADR-007) under a fail-open policy that mathematically cannot be authoritative — risking silent loss of PRD-mandated OBS-001/OBS-004 data. A third critical: the LangGraph PostgresSaver checkpoint and the app repository both write pipeline state to the same DB with no stated ownership/projection direction, so the "single-writer" claim is sound only at the process level, not the logical level. The important findings (Postgres<->filesystem reconciliation, worker write ownership, registry config-vs-DB authority, entity-count/source-of-truth-column conflation) are all resolvable with explicit ownership statements in ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2/§6.3/§6.5/§6.6/§7 and a rewrite of DATA_MODEL's Source-of-Truth column into two columns (owning entity vs physical store). Recommend the human confirm the Postgres-vs-local-store and Trace-authority decisions before /arch-finalize writes the binding contract — both are load-bearing and currently contradictory rather than merely thin.

findings.finding: Donor licensing (extracting EA donor packages from the user's own Sims 4 install and shipping derivative .package files) is asserted as the licensing solution ('Donors sourced from the user's own game install at runtime (licensing)') but is NEVER actually verified against EA's TOU/EULA or the Sims modding-community norms. It is treated as a settled fact, not a research item. This is the only legal/compliance dependency in the whole system and it underpins the entire export subsystem (ADR-05) plus the in-app distribution model ('shareable build for a few known users', §16). 'Sourced from the user's install' mitigates redistribution of EA *binaries*, but the product ships .package files that are derivative works grafting cloned EA OBJD/tuning/FTPT/RIG/SLOT resources — that is a different and unexamined question. No ADR, no RISKS row, no source citation.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md R-003 line 39 + ADR-005 line 67 both state 'Donors sourced from the user's own game install at runtime (licensing)' as a parenthetical assertion. RISKS.md has no licensing/legal/EULA/IP risk row (R1–R16 are all technical/operational; the 'Export ↔ user's Sims 4 install' trust boundary covers file-clobbering, not IP). CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF.md 'still-open items' (lines 57-65) lists 6 verify-first items — none is licensing. PRD §10/§24 require shipping installable content but say nothing about distribution rights.
findings.proposedFix: Add an ADR (or RISKS row + open question) on derivative-content licensing: verify that (a) cloning EA tuning/OBJD resources into a shipped .package is consistent with EA's UGC/modding policy and the de-facto S4S/Sims-modding norms, and (b) the 'shareable build' distribution model does not redistribute EA-owned resource bytes. If unresolved, gate it as a load-bearing human/legal decision before S1, since the clone-a-donor approach (ADR-05) has no non-derivative fallback.

findings.finding: The single most load-bearing external-dependency unknown — a headless Blender-5 Mac path from mesh → valid Sims-4 GEOM — has NO verified solution and ALL THREE named fallbacks are themselves unverified vapor. RESEARCH R-008 admits the only candidate exporters are GUI/old-Blender-bound (S4S 2.70–2.79; SmugTomato is Sims-3; 'SimGeom' has 'no canonical repo'). The fallbacks are: (1) 'pinned-old-Blender GEOM microservice' — but the old-Blender exporters are GUI add-ons, not headless, so this is not demonstrated to work headless either; (2) 'custom GEOM writer (s4py/s4sdk)' — s4py is described elsewhere as 'weak/dormant'; (3) 'Windows helper VM' — contradicts the Mac-first, single-binary-app deployment posture. So the export gate rests on a chain of unverified options where even the fallbacks are unproven.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md R-008 line 73: 'no maintained, headless, Blender-5 Sims-4 GEOM exporter exists … SimGeom with no canonical repo'; line 76 lists the three fallbacks as unproven. R-003 line 41: 'HIGH on the mesh half — no verified headless Mac GEOM authoring'. s4py called 'weak/dormant' in R-003 line 38. RISKS R1 is rated Critical/High and is the #1 spike, but the architecture (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.5, §15) still presents GEOM export as an in-scope subsystem rather than an unproven feasibility gate.
findings.proposedFix: Make explicit in ARCHITECTURE.md that NO viable GEOM path is yet verified and that S1 is a true go/no-go feasibility gate, not an implementation task — including a sub-spike that verifies at least ONE fallback actually runs headless on Mac (e.g., confirm a pinned-old-Blender exporter can run --background, or write+round-trip a minimal custom GEOM via s4py against an in-game test-install) BEFORE any downstream stage is built. Carry the 'no fallback proven headless' status as an open load-bearing risk.

findings.finding: OpenRouter is listed as a first-class image-to-3D / image-gen alternate provider in multiple places, but RESEARCH never verifies OpenRouter actually serves image-to-3D (or even image generation) models — and the handoff itself flags this as unverified ('it routes LLM/image, not necessarily 3D'). The draft architecture §9 lists 'Replicate/fal/OpenRouter alternates' for concept image gen as if confirmed, and ADR-04 lists OpenRouter among ImageGenProvider providers. OpenRouter is an LLM router; image and 3D coverage is unconfirmed. If a builder wires an OpenRouter image/3D adapter expecting parity with fal/WaveSpeed, it may not exist.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF.md line 63: 'OpenRouter image-to-3D coverage — verify (it routes LLM/image, not necessarily 3D)'. PRESEARCH.md line 125: '(Note: OpenRouter routes LLM/image...)' — qualifier present. But ADR-004 line 58 and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §9 line 168 list OpenRouter as an image-gen alternate without the caveat; RESEARCH R-009 line 80 says FLUX.2 is 'OpenRouter-style' (hedged, not confirmed). No RESEARCH finding confirms an OpenRouter image-to-3D endpoint at all.
findings.proposedFix: Demote OpenRouter to LLM-only (its verified role, ADR-14) in the architecture. Remove or explicitly mark-as-unverified its appearance as an ImageGenProvider/Image3DProvider alternate; if image-gen via OpenRouter is wanted, add a one-line spike to confirm coverage before listing it as a fallback the design relies on.

findings.finding: Provider pricing/output-format volatility is acknowledged at the top of RESEARCH ('Prices/versions change — re-verify at integration time') and RISKS R5 covers cost blowups, but there is NO re-verification gate or owner placed in the architecture for the specific volatile load-bearing facts the design depends on: FLUX.2's transparent_bg availability per endpoint, Tripo's 24h URL expiry window, fal model-id stability, and per-gen prices that feed the soft-budget estimator (REQ-NF-103). The soft-budget feature is must-ship and depends on per-adapter cost metadata that is explicitly volatile, yet nothing schedules a re-verify or marks the cost numbers as needing a refresh pass.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md line 5: 'Prices/versions change — re-verify at integration time'. R-009 line 83: 'Prices/transparent_bg availability vary by endpoint (re-verify)'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.4 'Cost metadata per op' + §11 'soft-budget warning' + REQ-NF-103 (PRESEARCH line 309) make cost data must-ship, but §9/§6.4 cite no mechanism to keep the volatile per-provider cost/format facts current; RISKS R5 mitigation is runtime cost capture, not a pre-build re-verification of the assumed numbers.
findings.proposedFix: Add an explicit 'integration-time re-verification' checklist item (owner + when) for the volatile provider facts the design hard-depends on: transparent_bg per chosen endpoint, Tripo URL TTL, fal model-ids, and seed per-gen prices for the estimator. Make the cost-metadata layer config-driven (already implied) and note the seed numbers are point-in-time and must be re-pulled at adapter-build time.

findings.finding: @s4tk longevity/provenance risk is identified (pre-release 0.x, last update 2024, single-maintainer, no first-class GEOM model) but the mitigation 'vendor-pin' is treated as sufficient, while the architecture simultaneously relies on @s4tk's resource ENCODERS as the basis for the custom-DBPF-writer fallback (ADR-05: 'custom ZLIB-only DBPF writer reusing s4tk encoders'). If @s4tk is abandoned AND a needed resource type/format proves missing or wrong, both the primary AND the named fallback share the same unmaintained dependency — the fallback is not independent. Also: @s4tk 'last update 2024' against a game patched in 2025-2026 means format coverage may already be stale, and no round-trip-against-current-game verification is gated before committing the export subsystem.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md R-003 line 38: '@s4tk … pre-release 0.x (last update 2024) — must vendor-pin … no first-class GEOM model'; line 41 fallback 'custom ZLIB-only DBPF writer reusing s4tk resource encoders'. ADR-005 line 69 repeats the same shared-dependency fallback. RISKS R7 (EA-patch drift) mitigates donors but not the s4tk library's own staleness vs the current game version. CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF line 64 flags '@s4tk pre-release; GEOM provenance — vendor-pin + round-trip CI' but no spike gates this before build.
findings.proposedFix: In S1, add an acceptance check that @s4tk (pinned version) round-trips a donor from the CURRENT game version losslessly (test-install confirms placeability) before the export subsystem is built on it. Note in the ADR that the custom-writer fallback shares the s4tk encoder dependency and is therefore NOT failure-independent for an abandonment scenario; if true independence is needed, the fallback must be the DBPF spec + own encoders.

findings.finding: The local-MPS image-to-3D fork (TRELLIS.2 MPS port, shivampkumar/trellis-mac) is correctly flagged as a 'young single-maintainer fork' with 'texture baking stubbed' and feature-flagged behind a pin+smoke-test — this one is handled well. The only residual gap: it is a single pinned community commit with no second fully-verified Mac fallback for the geometry-only path either (SF3D/SPAR3D MPS are called 'experimental'), so 'drop local entirely' is effectively the real fallback. That's acceptable given ADR-11's cloud-first stance, but the architecture should state plainly that local-3D has effectively no production-grade fallback and is genuinely optional/disposable.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md R-002 line 31-34: TRELLIS.2 MPS port is 'young single-maintainer fork, weak texturing'; SF3D/SPAR3D MPS 'experimental'; 'else drop local entirely'. ADR-011 line 122-125 keeps it feature-flagged/optional. RISKS R12 rates it Low severity. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6 'optional geometry-only local MPS fallback (feature-flagged)'.
findings.proposedFix: No load-bearing change needed; optionally make explicit in §6/ADR-11 that the local-3D path has no production-grade fallback (SF3D/SPAR3D are experimental), so its only real fallback is removal — keeping it strictly behind a feature flag and out of any acceptance-critical path.

findings.finding: Claude subscription/OAuth auth feasibility is the best-handled open item: ADR-14 explicitly flags it 'research required', states it is 'likely not a supported path', and instructs 'do NOT architect around it as the primary auth' with API-key as the realistic default. This is correctly de-risked. Minor residual: the auth-preference ORDER still lists 'Claude subscription/OAuth (if feasible)' FIRST, which a literal-minded implementer could try to wire first; the prose caveat and the table ('API-key auth (subscription=research)') resolve it, so impact is low.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md ADR-014 lines 140-142: preference order lists subscription first but the ⚠️ feasibility flag says 'likely not a supported path … do not architect around it as the primary auth'. CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF line 60-61 reinforces 'default to Anthropic API key / OpenRouter. Verify, don't architect around the subscription.'
findings.proposedFix: Optionally invert the stated preference order in ARCHITECTURE.md so API-key is listed first (with subscription as a flagged later experiment), eliminating any ambiguity for the implementer. No deeper change required.

external-deps.notes: Audited the external-deps dimension against RESEARCH.md (R-001..010), DECISIONS.md (ADR-001..014), RISKS.md, PRESEARCH.md, the architecture draft, and the PRD, under the production-grade adversarial posture. Overall the planning pass did a credible job: most external deps are flagged with fallbacks + invalidation conditions, and three of the prompt's eight named items (Claude subscription-auth, local-MPS fork viability, EA-patch drift via R7) are genuinely well-de-risked. But under production-grade scrutiny several load-bearing items are asserted-as-solved rather than verified, or have non-independent / unproven fallbacks. The two CRITICAL findings: (1) donor LICENSING — the only legal dependency in the system — is asserted in a parenthetical ('(licensing)') with zero verification, no ADR, and no RISKS row, yet it underpins the entire clone-a-donor export model and the in-app distribution plan; and (2) the headless Mac GEOM path is unverified AND all three named fallbacks (old-Blender microservice, custom s4py/s4sdk writer, Windows VM) are themselves unproven-headless or contradict the deployment posture, so the export gate rests on a chain of vapor — S1 must be framed as a true go/no-go that proves at least one fallback runs headless before anything downstream is built. IMPORTANT findings: OpenRouter image/3D coverage is listed as a relied-upon alternate but is unverified (handoff itself flags it); provider pricing/format volatility (transparent_bg per endpoint, Tripo 24h TTL, fal model-ids, seed prices feeding the must-ship soft-budget estimator) has no placed re-verification gate; and the @s4tk custom-writer fallback shares the same unmaintained library as the primary, so it is not failure-independent, plus @s4tk's 'last update 2024' vs a 2025-26-patched game means a current-version round-trip should gate S1. Claude-subscription auth and local-MPS are essentially clean (downgraded to nice-to-have).
