findings.finding: ADR-002 locks `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres`, but the ONLY research that informs it (R-005) exclusively researched and recommended `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite`. The Postgres-for-checkpoints choice rests entirely on ADR-009 (a separate app-data-store decision the checkpointer research never contemplated), not on any evaluation of PostgresSaver maturity/lifecycle/concurrency under a desktop-bundled Postgres. The 'one DB for app data + checkpoints' rationale silently overrode the researched SQLite path without re-research. Compounding evidence the design was reasoned about SQLite and not re-derived for Postgres: ADR-002 still mandates a 'single-writer lock' (a SQLite single-writer limitation) even though Postgres natively supports concurrent writers.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md R-005 line 54 'Recommendation: LangGraph 1.x + langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite, pinned together' and line 52 'Native local SQLite checkpointer' (PostgresSaver never mentioned); DECISIONS.md ADR-002 line 41 'LangGraph 1.x + langgraph-checkpoint-postgres ... aligns with ADR-009's Postgres store'; ADR-002 'single-writer lock' carried from R-005's 'SQLite single-writer' note (R-005 line 55).
findings.proposedFix: Either (a) re-base ADR-002 on SQLite (the researched/recommended path) and let ADR-009's Postgres host only the app relational data, or (b) keep PostgresSaver but add an explicit research/verification line confirming langgraph-checkpoint-postgres maturity + concurrency model on bundled desktop Postgres, and re-justify (or drop) the single-writer lock given Postgres concurrent writes. Brain 2 must force a human decision on which DB owns the checkpoint.

findings.finding: ADR-007 contains two mutually contradictory Decision blocks. The ADR is stamped 'Locked (user) — LangSmith (hosted SaaS)' with a 'Decision (final): LangSmith hosted' block, but later in the SAME ADR a second '**Decision:**' line states 'Instrument with OpenTelemetry (backend swappable). Backend = user decision (in discussion).' One says LangSmith is final/locked; the other says the backend is still in discussion and instrumentation is generic OTel. This is an unresolved/unlocked decision presented as Locked.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md ADR-007: status line 82 'Locked (user) — LangSmith (hosted SaaS, cloud tier)'; 'Decision (final)' line 84 'LangSmith hosted'; contradictory second 'Decision:' line 92 'Instrument with OpenTelemetry (backend swappable). Backend = user decision (in discussion).'
findings.proposedFix: Delete or clearly demote the stale '(in discussion)' OTel-backend Decision block to the 'options considered (record)' section so ADR-007 has exactly one binding Decision. If LangSmith is truly locked, say so once and remove the contradiction before finalize.

findings.finding: The LangSmith-SaaS-vs-local-first tension's stated mitigation (cheap swap to local Phoenix/Langfuse because 'the common path is OTel') is partly false given ADR-008. ADR-008 deliberately chose LangSmith-NATIVE evals (datasets, evaluate_comparative, annotation queues, @pytest.mark.langsmith) BECAUSE LangSmith was locked, and explicitly rejected the OTel-portable alternatives (Braintrust/Langfuse 'redundant'). So swapping the observability backend off LangSmith would also break the eval backbone — a tighter coupling than ADR-007/RISKS R6 acknowledge.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md ADR-007 line 84 'thin tracing seam so Phoenix/Langfuse (local) stay low-cost swaps'; ADR-008 line 100 backbone = 'LangSmith-native evals ... @pytest.mark.langsmith CI gating ... Reuses the locked LangSmith+LangGraph' and line 104 'Avoid: ... Braintrust/Langfuse (redundant 2nd platform vs locked LangSmith)'; RISKS.md R6 mitigation 'thin tracing seam (swap to Phoenix/Langfuse)'.
findings.proposedFix: Reconcile ADR-007 and ADR-008: state explicitly that observability-backend portability (OTel) and eval-backbone portability are DIFFERENT seams, and that abandoning LangSmith costs an eval-runner migration (ADR-008's documented DeepEval/Inspect AI fallback). Update R6's mitigation wording so the 'swap to local' claim is scoped to tracing only.

findings.finding: The bpy-vs-CLI Blender execution decision is presented as Locked in ADR-006 and the draft, but the source research explicitly left it for Brain 2 to confirm. R-008's synthesis note records an unreconciled conflict between R-008 (leaned bpy-core) and R-006 (leaned CLI-subprocess) and says the reconciliation toward CLI-primary is for 'Brain 2 to confirm' — i.e. a load-bearing decision the research deferred and the ADR silently closed.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md R-008 line 75 '(Synthesis note: R-008 leaned bpy-core, R-006 leaned CLI-subprocess; reconciled toward CLI-subprocess-primary — Brain 2 to confirm.)'; DECISIONS.md ADR-006 line 76 presents 'CLI-subprocess as the production execution path' as Locked; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md line 62 '06 | Blender = CLI-subprocess primary'.
findings.proposedFix: Brain 2 (finalize) must explicitly confirm CLI-subprocess-primary and record the confirmation in the ADR, OR keep it spike-gated (GEOM spike S1 already exists) and mark the bpy-vs-CLI execution path as 'confirmed at spike' rather than pre-locked. Remove the unaddressed 'Brain 2 to confirm' so the lock is honest.

findings.finding: Default-provider drift between RESEARCH recommendations and the ADRs. Image-to-3D: R-001 recommends 'First real adapter = fal + Tripo3D v2.5 default' (single default), but ADR-003 promotes 'two co-primary defaults: Hunyuan3D-2.x and Tripo3D v2.5' — Hunyuan3D-2.x was not the research's first-adapter pick and R-001 flagged it as dense-triangle 'needs decimate'. Concept image: R-009 and draft §9 both say 'WaveSpeed default', but the draft §3 ADR-04 summary line omits any default provider and ADR-004's text states the default provider-agnostically, so 'the default provider' is asserted inconsistently across draft §3 / draft §9 / ADR-004.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md R-001 line 26 'First real adapter = fal + Tripo3D v2.5 default'; DECISIONS.md ADR-003 line 50 'Two co-primary defaults: Hunyuan3D-2.x and Tripo3D v2.5'; R-009 line 81 'WaveSpeed default' and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md line 168 'WaveSpeed default' vs draft line 60 ADR-04 summary (no provider default) and DECISIONS.md ADR-004 line 58 (provider-agnostic).
findings.proposedFix: Pick one image-to-3D first-adapter default (research said Tripo v2.5) and state it as the seed while keeping the bakeoff open; reconcile the 'co-primary' framing with R-001's single-default recommendation. For concept image, state 'WaveSpeed = seed default provider' consistently in ADR-004 and both draft summary and §9.

findings.finding: DATA_MODEL.md's store-of-truth language contradicts the Postgres lock (ADR-009). Its header still declares 'Source of truth = the local project store (per-project folder on disk; a project DB/JSON index + artifact files)' and every relational entity is tagged 'local store' — language that pre-dates the app-managed-Postgres decision. A reader cross-checking DATA_MODEL against ADR-009/draft §7 hits a direct contradiction (JSON-index-on-disk vs Postgres).
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md lines 5-6 'Source of truth = the local project store (per-project folder on disk; a project DB/JSON index + artifact files)'; contradicts DECISIONS.md ADR-009 line 111 'App-managed local Postgres as the relational/state store' and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 154.
findings.proposedFix: Update DATA_MODEL.md's header and 'Source of Truth' column to reference app-managed Postgres + filesystem artifacts (per ADR-009), or add a one-line note that physical storage is Postgres per ADR-009 and 'local store' here means logical ownership.

findings.finding: Entity-count is inconsistent across docs. Draft §5 and PRESEARCH §5 both say '16 entities'; PRESEARCH Phase-0 intake says '11 product entities (§20)'; DATA_MODEL.md actually defines 20 entities (Project … ProviderConfig/Secret). No single number is correct in the draft.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md line 115 '16 entities'; PRESEARCH.md line 283 '16 entities' and line 68 '11 product entities (§20)'; DATA_MODEL.md lines 13-32 enumerate 20 entities.
findings.proposedFix: Recount and state the real number (20) consistently in draft §5 and PRESEARCH, or drop the count and just reference DATA_MODEL.md as canonical.

findings.finding: ADR-014 is stamped 'Locked (user)' yet its stated preferred auth path (Claude subscription/OAuth) carries a strong 'research required / likely not a supported path' feasibility flag. The decision is well-handled (realistic default = API key, which is sound), but the only surviving carrier of the verify-first caveat in the summary view is the terse '(subscription = research)' note; a reader scanning the Locked-Decision Summary table could miss that the preferred-order top entry is explicitly not architected-around.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md ADR-014 line 141 'Claude subscription/OAuth auth ... likely not a supported path ... Treat "use the subscription" as a verify-first item; do not architect around it as the primary auth'; summary table line 24 '(subscription=research)'.
findings.proposedFix: In the ADR-014 Decision line, make the binding default explicitly 'Anthropic API key (or OpenRouter)' and demote subscription/OAuth to an explicitly-flagged research item, so 'Locked' applies to the API-key path and the unverified subscription path is not implied to be locked.

decisions-consistency.notes: Audited DECISIONS.md (ADR-001..014) against ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md, PRESEARCH.md, RESEARCH.md, DATA_MODEL.md, RISKS.md, and the PRD. The dimension is NOT clean — there are two genuine contradictions that are load-bearing. (1) The Postgres-vs-SQLite checkpointer tension is the most serious: every piece of research (R-005) recommends SQLite and the SQLite-derived 'single-writer lock' survives into the Postgres decision, yet ADR-002 locks PostgresSaver purely on the strength of ADR-009's separate store choice, with zero checkpointer-on-Postgres research — a decision that needs a human re-confirm. (2) ADR-007 literally contains two contradictory Decision blocks (LangSmith 'final/locked' vs 'backend = user decision, in discussion'); finalize must pick one. The LangSmith-SaaS-vs-local-first tension IS acknowledged (RISKS R6, ADR-007 fail-open), but ADR-008's choice of LangSmith-NATIVE evals quietly tightens the coupling so the 'cheap swap to local' fallback is only true for tracing, not evals. The bpy-vs-CLI Blender reconciliation is presented as Locked but RESEARCH R-008 explicitly defers it to 'Brain 2 to confirm' — so finalize must actually confirm it rather than inherit a pre-closed lock. Remaining findings are provider-default drift (Tripo single-default in research vs Hunyuan+Tripo co-primary in ADR-003; WaveSpeed-default stated inconsistently) and three cosmetic-but-real cross-doc inconsistencies (DATA_MODEL still says on-disk JSON-index source-of-truth contradicting the Postgres lock; entity count 16 vs 11 vs actual 20; ADR-014 'Locked' wrapping a verify-first auth path). Draft claims are otherwise well-backed by ADRs — the locked-decision summary table and §3 are internally consistent with the ADR bodies; the gaps are between the ADRs and their cited research, and the two intra-ADR contradictions above.

findings.finding: The 'spikes-first' sequencing is asserted everywhere but is NOWHERE defined as an enforceable GATE. No artifact specifies (a) the pass/fail exit criteria for S1/S2/S3, (b) what each spike BLOCKS if it fails, or (c) the abort/descope decision the human makes on a spike failure. It is consistently worded as ordering/recommendation ('must precede breadth', 'sequenced first', 'spike-gated'), never as a hard precondition with a kill-switch. Because S1 (GEOM/DBPF export) is the gating feasibility unknown for the ENTIRE product (assumption A2 = 'most dangerous'), the absence of a real gate means downstream breadth could be built before feasibility is proven — exactly the overbuild RISKS.md R14 warns about.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18 'Spikes-first (must precede breadth): S1...S2...S3' and §1 'sequenced behind de-risking spikes first' state ordering only. §4A lists Tracks A–F as 'Independent parallel build tracks (after contracts freeze)' and tags Tracks C/D merely '*spike-gated*' with no exit criteria. ADR-012 says 'Spikes-first sequencing' with no gate definition. RISKS.md R1 mitigation = 'Spike S1 first ... or trigger a fallback' but the trigger condition is unspecified. CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF says 'Nothing downstream is real until this is settled' — an assertion, not an encoded gate. ADR-006 invalidation: 'spike finds no viable headless GEOM path → escalate to a fallback (added scope)' but no defined decision point.
findings.proposedFix: In the binding ARCHITECTURE.md, convert spikes-first into an explicit gate: for each of S1/S2/S3 specify (1) a binary PASS criterion (e.g., S1 PASS = '@s4tk clone-a-donor + headless GEOM produces an object that places in Build/Buy via test-install on a clean Mac'), (2) the exact set of tasks/tracks BLOCKED until PASS (S1 blocks all of Track C breadth beyond one donor, all export-dependent acceptance criteria, and any functional breadth), and (3) the named fallback each failure triggers plus a human decision checkpoint. Have /tasks-gen emit these as gate tasks that downstream tasks declare a dependency on.

findings.finding: The open-ceiling scope ('functional archetypes as many as feasible' + 'decorative breadth unlimited' + 'full-fidelity / real-and-placeable for ALL exported items') combined with no timebox has no concrete floor/ceiling or stop condition for the FIRST correct build. There is no defined minimum acceptance set (e.g., 'N decorative items + exactly 1 functional archetype proven in-game') that constitutes 'done enough to stop expanding.' This is the precise overbuild risk PRD §28.6 names, and the architecture acknowledges R14 but does not constrain it — it only points back to acceptance criteria that themselves describe the full-fidelity ceiling.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §1a G2 'real, in-game-placeable output for *all* exported items' and G3 'as many as feasible'; §18 'Open ceiling: decorative breadth unlimited; functional archetypes "as many as feasible."' RISKS.md R14 'Scope creep / overbuild ... given open ceiling + no timebox' Sev=Med, mitigation 'anchor-bound tasks; registry seeds proven set first' — but no first-build floor is defined. PRESEARCH Phase 7 'Timebox: none — correctness-first ... Removes the main pressure to cut the full-fidelity scope' explicitly removes the natural brake. PRD §28.6 mitigation 1 'Use MVP feature list as boundary' is undercut because the locked scope ELEVATED the PRD's bounded '4 functional archetypes / 7 categories' into open registries (PRESEARCH Phase 1 'SCOPE-ELEVATING').
findings.proposedFix: Pin an explicit 'first correct build' definition in ARCHITECTURE.md §18 / §2 that is the stop-line before breadth: the Y2K anchor set end-to-end + exactly ONE functional archetype proven in-game (matching PRD §6.2 / AC-013 as originally written) = the acceptance floor; everything past it (additional archetypes, additional placement types) is post-floor registry expansion explicitly gated on S3 PASS and a human go-ahead. Make the 'real-and-placeable for ALL items' bar apply to the anchor set first, not be a precondition for the first build to count.

findings.finding: Several subsystems were scope-ELEVATED beyond the PRD baseline and locked as must-ship, but the cumulative overbuild risk of doing all of them before the gating spike (S1) passes is not surfaced. Specifically: app-managed bundled Postgres + pgvector (ADR-009), multi-swatch generation+export (REQ-F-104), bounded-parallel job engine distinct from the graph (REQ-NF-101), deep-sign/notarize macOS packaging of nested binaries (§16/R4), and a 9-harness eval layer with a custom mesh-metric component layer (ADR-008). Each is individually justified by the production-grade posture, but none is gated behind S1, so substantial production infrastructure could be fully built for a product whose core export feasibility is still unproven.
findings.evidence: ADR-009 locks bundled Postgres+pgvector with its own admission 'Tradeoff/Risk: bundling + signing/notarizing a Postgres binary on macOS adds packaging weight'; the lighter SQLite fallback exists but is not the starting point. REQ-F-104 multi-swatch 'must-ship', PRESEARCH Phase 8 'Multi-swatch generation + export ... must-handle'. §16 + RISKS R4 (Sev=High, Like=High) macOS notarization of sidecar+Postgres+Blender. ADR-008 'metric component layer (framework-agnostic — the real engineering)'. None of these declare a dependency on S1 PASS in §4A's parallel-track list.
findings.proposedFix: Sequence the heavy production infrastructure relative to S1: explicitly allow Tracks A/B/F to proceed on mocks + SQLite/lighter store, but flag bundled-Postgres, multi-swatch export, and full notarization pipeline as 'build after S1 PASS' (or behind a feature flag) so the most expensive infra isn't completed before core feasibility. Note pgvector is reserved for future preference learning (DATA_MODEL) and could be deferred without losing the MVP.

findings.finding: The locked scope contradicts the PRD's own anti-overbuild guardrails without flagging the contradiction. PRD §27 guardrail 18 ('Avoid over-scoping') and §28.6 mitigation 1 ('Use MVP feature list as boundary') treat the PRD's bounded 7 categories / 4 functional archetypes as the boundary; the planning chain replaced that boundary with open registries and 'as many as feasible' (ADR-010, PRESEARCH Phase 1). This may be a legitimate user-confirmed reframe, but the architecture presents it as settled without acknowledging it directly overrides a PRD overbuild guardrail — which is the one thing this dimension is told to scrutinize.
findings.evidence: PRD §27.18 'Avoid over-scoping into CAS, animation, or arbitrary gameplay mods' and §28.6.1 'Use MVP feature list as boundary'; §8.2/§9.2 define the bounded category/archetype lists. ADR-010 'No fixed enums ... Functional behavior seeded "as many as feasible."' is marked 'Locked (user, Phase-10 reframe)'. PRESEARCH Phase 1 explicitly labels these 'SCOPE-ELEVATING'. The ARCHITECTURE draft §18 states the open ceiling as fact with no note that it supersedes a PRD guardrail.
findings.proposedFix: Add an explicit reconciliation note in ARCHITECTURE.md §18 (and a cross-reference in §2) stating that the open-registry / 'as many as feasible' scope is a deliberate user-confirmed override of PRD §27.18 / §28.6, justified by no-timebox + registry-extensibility, AND bounded by: (a) registries SEED only the proven set, (b) breadth expansion is gated on the corresponding spike, (c) the out-of-scope frontier (novel scripted gameplay) is unchanged. This keeps the override honest and bounded rather than silently broadening scope.

This is a stale-doc drift, not a scope decision, but it muddies what durability/migration surface (Alembic vs JSON index) is actually in scope.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md header: 'Source of truth = the local project store (per-project folder on disk; a project DB/JSON index + artifact files).' vs ADR-009 'App-managed local Postgres ... Alembic migrations' and ARCHITECTURE §7 'Source of truth = app-managed Postgres'.
findings.proposedFix: Update DATA_MODEL.md's source-of-truth line to match ADR-009 (Postgres + files), or add a note that 'local project store' = Postgres + artifact files, so the durability/migration scope (Alembic, pg_dump backup) is unambiguous downstream.

scope-balance.notes: Dimension audited: scope-balance (8 + 8a) against the production-grade, narrow-but-open posture. The dimension is NOT clean. Two CRITICAL load-bearing gaps dominate: (1) 'spikes-first' is asserted in five places but never encoded as an enforceable gate with pass/fail criteria, blocked-task sets, or a fallback/abort decision point — so the central feasibility de-risking mechanism is decorative, not binding; and (2) the open-ceiling + no-timebox scope has no defined first-build floor/stop-line, which is exactly the PRD §28.6 / RISKS R14 overbuild risk left unconstrained. Two IMPORTANT findings: heavy production infra (bundled Postgres, multi-swatch, notarization, 9-harness eval layer) is not sequenced behind S1 so it could be fully built before core feasibility is proven; and the open-registry reframe directly overrides PRD §27.18/§28.6 guardrails without flagging the override. UNDER-BUILD note: production concerns themselves (idempotency R9, reconcile-resume REQ-NF-102, fail-open observability REQ-O-102, keychain secrets R11, trust boundaries, error taxonomy, durability) are actually well-covered — they are present and mapped — so the under-built side of this dimension is largely satisfied; the imbalance is on the OVERBUILD/sequencing side, not missing production hygiene. The single non-load-bearing nit is a stale source-of-truth line in DATA_MODEL.md. findings.finding: EVAL-004's stated purpose is now partly unsatisfiable: the PRD requires the Blender Automation Harness to "compare deterministic Python, MCP agentic control, and hybrid cleanup" (PRD §19.4), but ADR-006/§3 row 06 LOCK 'MCP excluded' from the Blender stage. The architecture never reconciles this — §14 just asserts '9 harnesses EVAL-001…009 map to the stages' without acknowledging that one of EVAL-004's three comparison arms (MCP) has been removed by decision. As written, an implementer cannot build EVAL-004 to spec, and there is no restated pass criteria for what EVAL-004 now compares (CLI-subprocess vs bpy-in-process per ADR-006, with hybrid-repair).
findings.evidence: PRD §19.4 EVAL-004 'Compare deterministic Python, MCP agentic control, and hybrid cleanup'; ADR-006 'MCP excluded' + DECISIONS summary row 06 'MCP excluded'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 only says '9 harnesses ... map to the stages' with no per-harness restatement; EVAL-004 PRD pass criteria are import/orientation/scale/origin/materials/render/export/structured-failure (still valid) but the comparison axis is now mis-specified.
findings.proposedFix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §14, restate EVAL-004 explicitly: comparison arms are now {CLI-subprocess (production path) vs bpy-in-process (spike/iteration)} plus deterministic-core-vs-hybrid-repair, and record that MCP is dropped as a stage executor (ADR-006) and at most a manual dev-only rescue — not part of EVAL-004. Add a per-harness EVAL→stage→metric→runner mapping table so each of the 9 is individually pinned, not asserted in aggregate.

findings.finding: The eval render bridge has an unacknowledged bootstrap/circular dependency that can make EVAL-002/003 untestable for the entire pre-spike period. ADR-008 states image-to-3D fidelity metrics MUST go through the 'Blender --background multi-view render → image metrics' bridge because 'headless GPU offscreen via pyrender/Open3D is broken on Apple Silicon → reuse the Blender stage as the render bridge.' But the Blender stage (Track D) is spike-gated (S1) and §4A marks Tracks C and D as '*spike-gated*'. So EVAL-003 (the image-to-3D bakeoff that is itself spike S2 and is supposed to PICK the model) cannot produce its appearance/fidelity metrics until the Blender render path exists — yet the Blender render path is being de-risked in S1 in parallel. The architecture never sequences the render-bridge as a prerequisite of EVAL-002/003, nor offers a fallback metric when the bridge is unavailable.
findings.evidence: ADR-008 metric layer: 'image-to-3D fidelity = Blender --background multi-view render → image metrics (⚠️ headless GPU offscreen ... broken on Apple Silicon → reuse the Blender stage as the render bridge)'; §4A 'Track C ... *spike-gated*' / 'Track D ... *spike-gated*'; CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF build order puts S1 (DBPF/GEOM, which includes the Blender path) and S2 (image-to-3D bakeoff) as separate spikes; §14 lists the render bridge as a caveat but gives no sequencing.
findings.proposedFix: In §14/§18 declare the Blender headless render bridge a hard prerequisite of EVAL-002/003 and sequence a minimal render-only Blender capability (no GEOM export needed) ahead of the S2 bakeoff. Specify the fallback fidelity signal when the bridge is down (e.g., concept-vs-thumbnail CLIP/SSIM on the provider's own preview render, flagged as lower-confidence) so the bakeoff is never fully blocked.

findings.finding: The two highest-value 'tests' (EVAL-007 functional in-game behavior, EVAL-008/REQ-O-101 test-install) are MANUAL human checks, not automated harnesses, yet they are the acceptance bar — and the architecture never defines what the AUTOMATED EVAL-007/008 harnesses assert in CI, nor how a no-Sims-install (R16) or headless-CI environment runs them. §14 mentions 'DBPF round-trip + test-install gate in validation' but test-install + in-game placeability/behavior is inherently manual (RISKS R1/R16, USER_FLOWS F 'manual in-game placeability/behavior check'). This leaves EVAL-007/008 as harnesses with no defined automatable pass criteria, so CI cannot gate on the project's actual definition of done.
findings.evidence: PRD §19.7 EVAL-007 pass criteria reference 'validation passes' but PRD §6.2/§26.2 + USER_FLOWS F require 'manual in-game placeability/behavior check'; RISKS R1 Test/Validation = 'DBPF round-trip + in-game test-install gate'; R16 'No Sims 4 install yet ... structure-only checks until then'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 names 'DBPF round-trip + test-install gate' but does not separate the automatable DBPF round-trip/parse-back assertion from the manual in-game step.
findings.proposedFix: Split each of EVAL-007/008 into (a) an automatable tier — DBPF round-trip (write→reparse with @s4tk→assert required resource set OBJD/COBJ/MODL/MLOD/GEOM/FTPT/RIG present, OBJD→tuning instance resolves, GEOM normals/UV/meshgroup-count match) runnable in headless CI without a game install; and (b) a manual gated tier — in-game test-install checklist run by the user. Define the structure-only validation path (R16) as the default CI gate and make in-game a release/anchor checkpoint. Pin this in §14 and §15.

findings.finding: Reference-mesh availability for Chamfer/Hausdorff/F-score is acknowledged as a constraint but never made concrete — there is no plan for WHERE the held-out reference meshes come from, who authors them, or what the benchmark set is. ADR-008 + §14 both say these metrics run 'only on a held-out benchmark set' / 'benchmark sets', but no artifact defines that benchmark set's contents, source (the 5 BLEND-001/§19.3 spike assets are concept images, not ground-truth 3D meshes), licensing, or storage (Git-LFS/DVC was mentioned in the superseded R-010 DeepEval plan but dropped in ADR-008). Without authored reference meshes, EVAL-003's most rigorous quantitative metric is dead on arrival and the bakeoff silently falls back to appearance-only.
findings.evidence: ADR-008 Caveats: 'Chamfer/Hausdorff/F-score need a reference mesh → use only on a held-out benchmark set; live generations score via appearance ...'; §14 'reference-mesh metrics only on benchmark sets'; PRD §19.3 EVAL-003 lists no reference-mesh source; the spike asset set (PRD §15.2 / §19.3) is concept images of Y2K props, not ground-truth meshes; R-010's 'goldens in Git-LFS/DVC' was part of the demoted DeepEval plan and not carried into ADR-008.
findings.proposedFix: Add to §14 a concrete reference-mesh plan: name the small benchmark set (e.g., 5–10 hand-authored or asset-store CC0 Sims-style props with known-good meshes), its license, its on-disk/DVC location, and who/what produces it; state explicitly that Chamfer/Hausdorff run ONLY on this set and that all live generations use self-consistency (watertight/normals/winding) + appearance render-compare. Without this, mark EVAL-003 quantitative-fidelity as deferred and say so.

findings.finding: Mock-adapter parity (PIPE-002/REQ-T-101) is asserted to enable 'full-flow tests without cloud' (§14), but the architecture never specifies the parity CONTRACT that makes this true — i.e., that mocks must emit the same async submit→poll→fetch state shapes, the same failure/timeout/expiry events, the same cost/latency metadata, and the same artifact lineage as real adapters. NFR §22.2.5 ('mock and real adapters must return consistent state shapes') is the requirement, but §6.4/§13 only say 'Mock + real behind one interface.' Crucially, the highest-risk full-flow behaviors (reconcile-and-resume R9, Tripo 24h URL expiry R8, two-phase submit/poll, provider outage J) are precisely the ones a naive synchronous mock would NOT exercise — so 'full-flow tests on mocks' could pass while the real reconcile/idempotency paths are untested.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 'mock adapters give full-flow tests without cloud'; §6.4 'Mock + real behind one interface (PIPE-002/003)'; NFR §22.2 item 5 'Mock and real adapters must return consistent state shapes'; RISKS R8 (URL expiry), R9 (resume double-exec) have Test/Validation = 'crash-mid-run → resume test' / 'kill-after-submit → no double-submit' — these need mocks that model async + injectable failures, not just happy-path stubs.
findings.proposedFix: In §14 (and the provider-interface contract in §6.4/§13) require mock adapters to be ASYNC-shaped and fault-injectable: simulate submit→pending→poll→succeeded/failed, configurable latency, timeouts, rate-limit/outage, and (for image-to-3D) URL-expiry — so reconcile-resume (R9), expiry-redownload (R8), and outage (Flow J) are exercised on mocks in CI. Add explicit contract tests asserting mock/real state-shape and event-sequence parity.

findings.finding: Contract tests are named but undefined, leaving the system's most important integration seams unverified. §14 says 'contract tests on the IPC + worker + provider interfaces' and §4A names five frozen-first contracts (IPC, domain types py⇄ts, provider, worker, registry), but no doc specifies HOW the py⇄ts domain-type sync (§13 'generated or hand-synced to TS') is verified to stay in sync, nor what the worker-contract tests assert (BlenderJob/ExportJob in/out), nor how SSE resumability (Last-Event-ID, §6.1) is tested. The py↔ts drift risk is real (PRESEARCH calls the IPC boundary a 'bug surface') and 'hand-synced' types with no enforcing test will silently diverge.
findings.evidence: §14 'contract tests on the IPC + worker + provider interfaces'; §4A 'Domain types/schemas ... pydantic (Python) ↔ TS types (UI/Node), kept in sync'; §13 'domain types/schemas ... generated or hand-synced to TS'; PRESEARCH Phase-0 'the Python↔UI IPC boundary becoming a bug surface'; §6.1 SSE 'resumable: Last-Event-ID' has no stated test.
findings.proposedFix: In §14 enumerate the contract-test set: (1) a schema-sync check that fails CI if pydantic and TS domain types diverge (prefer single-source generation over hand-sync); (2) worker-contract golden tests for BlenderJob/ExportJob input→output shapes incl. structured-error envelope; (3) IPC command/SSE-event schema validation + an SSE Last-Event-ID resume/replay test; (4) registry-schema validation tests (PlacementType/FunctionalArchetype/DonorMapping).

findings.finding: CI determinism and offline-eval execution are stated as goals but the mechanism is under-specified and partially self-contradictory with the fail-open/local-first posture. ADR-008/§14 require 'pin judge model + weights for CI determinism' and offline via 'LANGSMITH_TEST_TRACKING=false' / 'LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE', but: (a) the judge is Claude/OpenRouter (a NETWORK LLM call) — pinning a model id does not make a cloud judge deterministic or offline-runnable, so 'CI determinism' for any GEval/VLM-judge harness (EVAL-001 plan coherence, EVAL-002 style match, subjective tiers) is not actually achievable as described; (b) using @pytest.mark.langsmith ties eval execution to LangSmith availability, which conflicts with REQ-O-102 fail-open / R6 offline. The architecture never says which harnesses are deterministic-gating in CI vs directional/nightly-only.
findings.evidence: ADR-008 'Pin judge model + metric weights for CI determinism; cache weights for offline'; judge = 'Claude/OpenRouter inside plain-Python evaluators'; ADR-008 'Aesthetic/IQA models are noisy/biased → directional signals, never hard gates'; REQ-O-102 fail-open observability; RISKS R6 'offline run completes'; §14 caveat 'aesthetic/IQA = directional, never hard gates' but no list of which EVALs gate CI.
findings.proposedFix: In §14 classify each of the 9 harnesses as either deterministic-CI-gating (schema/structure/round-trip/mesh self-consistency — no LLM judge) or directional/nightly (anything using an LLM/VLM judge or IQA), and state that LLM-judge harnesses run nightly with cached responses (LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE) and never block the deterministic CI gate. Clarify that 'CI determinism' applies to the deterministic tier only; for judge tiers, pin model id + temperature=0 + cache, and treat results as monitored signals, not hard gates.

findings.finding: EVAL-009 (human-preference harness) and its storage substrate are not fully wired: ADR-008 maps it to LangSmith 'annotation queues' and §7 reserves pgvector 'for preference/similarity (OBS-004/EVAL-009)', but pgvector usage is explicitly 'future' and the local ReviewEvent store (DATA_MODEL) vs LangSmith feedback (ADR-007 'capture user accept/reject as LangSmith feedback/runs') are two parallel sinks with no stated single source of truth or reconciliation. With fail-open tracing, review events captured only to LangSmith could be lost on outage.
findings.evidence: ADR-008 EVAL-009 → 'annotation queues (human-preference)'; ADR-007 'Capture user accept/reject as LangSmith feedback/runs'; §7 'pgvector reserved for preference/similarity (OBS-004/EVAL-009)'; DATA_MODEL ReviewEvent 'append-only authoritative' in local store; REQ-O-102 fail-open means LangSmith may be unreachable.
findings.proposedFix: State in §7/§14 that ReviewEvent in local Postgres is the authoritative source for EVAL-009 (survives LangSmith outage per fail-open), and LangSmith annotation queues are a derived/optional mirror. Confirm whether pgvector preference learning is in-scope for MVP EVAL-009 or deferred; if deferred, say EVAL-009 = capture + export only.

testing.notes: Audited the testing/testability dimension against PRD §19 (EVAL-001..009), §23 (validation), §26 (acceptance), ADR-006/007/008, RESEARCH R-010/R-008/R-003, RISKS R1/R6/R8/R9/R16, USER_FLOWS F, and DATA_MODEL invariants. The eval STACK choice (LangSmith-native backbone + framework-agnostic metric component layer + pytest/pydantic/syrupy) is well-reasoned and the 'no framework has native 3D-mesh metrics' finding is correct and important. However the dimension is NOT clean: the architecture asserts '9 harnesses map to the stages' in aggregate (§14) without a per-harness EVAL→stage→metric→runner table, and that aggregate assertion hides four real problems. The three critical, load-bearing ones each need a human decision before finalize: (1) EVAL-004's PRD-mandated comparison axis (deterministic/MCP/hybrid) contradicts the ADR-006 MCP-exclusion lock and is never restated; (2) the mandatory Blender render bridge for EVAL-002/003 fidelity has a spike-gated bootstrap/circular dependency with no sequencing or fallback metric; (3) the acceptance-bar 'tests' (EVAL-007 in-game behavior, EVAL-008 test-install) are manual and lack a defined automatable CI tier, so CI cannot gate on the actual definition of done. The reference-mesh question (asked in my brief) is acknowledged but not concretized — no benchmark-set source/location/license, so Chamfer/Hausdorff is effectively undeliverable as written (important). Mock-adapter parity (PIPE-002) is claimed to enable full-flow tests w/o cloud, but the parity CONTRACT (async shape + fault injection for reconcile/expiry/outage — the very paths R8/R9/J need) is unspecified, so 'full-flow on mocks' risks green-on-mocks/broken-on-real. CI determinism is also overclaimed for LLM-judge harnesses (a cloud judge is neither deterministic nor offline). Recommend a per-harness mapping table + an explicit CI-gating-tier vs directional-tier classification be added to ARCHITECTURE.md §14 during finalize.

findings.finding: No rollback/downgrade story exists. Alembic is named for migrations (ARCH §7, ADR-009) but there is zero mention of downgrade() scripts, what happens when a user runs an OLDER app build against a data dir migrated by a NEWER build, or how to recover from a bad migration. Under production-grade posture, deploy/rollback is explicitly a critical concern (CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF 'Build Posture' lists 'deploy/rollback' as a critical gap class). REQ-D-101's acceptance signal only covers the forward direction ('older project opens after schema bump'); the reverse (downgrade) is unspecified, and a desktop app shipped to users WILL be downgraded (user reverts a bad update, or restores an old backup).
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 156 ('Alembic migrations; backup = copy folder + pg_dump') and §16; ADR-009 (DECISIONS.md:111) names Alembic but no downgrade path; REQ-D-101 acceptance signal (PRESEARCH.md:313) is forward-only; CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF.md lines 11-15 mandate auditing deploy/rollback as critical.
findings.proposedFix: In binding §7/§16 require: (1) every Alembic revision ships a tested downgrade(); (2) a pre-migration automatic DB snapshot (pg_dump or PGDATA copy) taken before any schema upgrade, with a documented restore command; (3) define the supported version-skew policy (e.g. 'app refuses to open a data dir migrated by a newer app version' — see data-dir-version finding) so an accidental downgrade fails safe instead of silently corrupting. Add an acceptance test: migrate up, run, downgrade, reopen with prior app build.

findings.finding: Data-dir / app-version compatibility is undefined. There is no version stamp written into the data dir, no compatibility check on startup, and no defined behavior when app version and on-disk schema version diverge. The LangGraph checkpointer SHARES the same Postgres (ADR-002/ADR-009), so a schema migration or an interrupted migration can corrupt or orphan IN-FLIGHT pipeline runs — directly colliding with the reconcile-and-resume guarantee (REQ-NF-102, System Flow I). The draft never reconciles 'migrate the DB on app update' with 'resume in-flight runs after reopen': what happens to a checkpoint written by app vN when app vN+1's migration changes the checkpoint tables?
findings.evidence: ADR-002 (DECISIONS.md:41) 'one DB for app data + checkpoints'; ADR-009 (DECISIONS.md:111) 'LangGraph PostgresSaver shares the same DB'; System Flow I (USER_FLOWS.md:112-116) reconcile-and-resume; REQ-NF-102 (PRESEARCH.md:308). No data-dir version stamp or compat gate appears anywhere in ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7/§16 or DATA_MODEL.md.
findings.proposedFix: Binding ARCHITECTURE must: (1) stamp the data dir with an app-version + schema-revision file and check it at startup, with explicit forward/back policy (open / migrate-with-snapshot / refuse); (2) specify that app updates DRAIN or quiesce in-flight runs before migrating (or that the checkpoint schema is migrated by the same Alembic head that the reconciler reads), and add a test: kill mid-run, update app (run migration), reopen → runs still reconcile or are cleanly marked needs-retry, never silently lost; (3) pin the langgraph-checkpoint-postgres schema version alongside the Alembic head.

findings.finding: Bundled-Postgres lifecycle and first-run init are essentially unaddressed, and Postgres MAJOR-version upgrades across app updates are a silent deploy landmine. ADR-009 says Postgres is 'bundled + lifecycle-managed (start/health/stop)' and REQ-O-103 covers start/health/restart/stop, but neither covers: first-run cluster creation (initdb), PGDATA location/permissions, the bundled PG binary version pin, OR what happens when an app update ships a new PG major version — PGDATA from PG N is NOT readable by PG N+1 without pg_upgrade. A user updating the app could find their entire local DB (all projects + checkpoints) unopenable.
findings.evidence: ADR-009 (DECISIONS.md:111-113) 'bundled + lifecycle-managed (start/health/stop)' with no initdb/PGDATA/version detail; REQ-O-103 (PRESEARCH.md:317) is start/health/restart/stop only; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6.8 (Supervisor) lists 'free-port selection, spawn, /health poll, supervised restart, teardown' — no init/upgrade; §16 line 222 only says 'Local data dir for Postgres + artifacts'.
findings.proposedFix: Binding §6.8/§16 must specify: (1) first-run initdb sequence (create cluster, set locale/encoding, restricted PGDATA perms, localhost/unix-socket-only bind); (2) the pinned PG major version recorded in the data dir; (3) a major-version-upgrade procedure on app update (detect PGDATA version mismatch → pg_dump-with-old-binary then restore-into-new, or bundle pg_upgrade, or refuse-and-instruct) with an automatic backup first. Add a clean-machine first-run smoke test AND a PG-major-bump upgrade test to acceptance.

findings.finding: The R4 notarization mitigation has a verification 'plan' that is too vague to be a verification plan. It says 'CI automates sign/notarize/staple early' and 'verify end-to-end on a clean Apple Silicon machine / clean-machine install smoke test' but never enumerates: which nested binaries must be deep-signed (PyInstaller .so/.framework/base_library.zip, the bundled Postgres binaries + libs, Blender if bundled, the Node @s4tk worker), the required entitlements/Hardened Runtime flags, or the concrete post-build verification commands. R-006 itself flags this as 'the highest-risk packaging task' that breaks 'unless EVERY nested binary is deep-signed' — yet the binding-bound text gives no checklist to verify against.
findings.evidence: R4 (RISKS.md:13) mitigation 'CI-automate sign/notarize/staple early; verify end-to-end... clean-machine install smoke test'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §16 lines 219-223; R-006 (RESEARCH.md:59) 'macOS notarization of the PyInstaller sidecar = highest-risk... unless every nested binary is deep-signed w/ Hardened Runtime'. Four bundled binary trees (sidecar, Postgres, Blender, Node worker) each need signing but none are enumerated as a signing inventory.
findings.proposedFix: In §16 add a notarization verification plan: (1) an explicit signing inventory of every nested binary tree (PyInstaller sidecar incl. base_library.zip/.so/.dylib, bundled Postgres + its lib/*.dylib + extensions like pgvector, Blender bundle if bundled, Node @s4tk worker) each deep-signed with Hardened Runtime + timestamp; (2) the entitlements file contents; (3) concrete CI verification gates that must pass: codesign --verify --deep --strict, spctl -a -vvv (Gatekeeper assess), stapler validate, and a launch test on a clean/quarantined-download VM. Make these CI gates, not prose.

findings.finding: Backup/restore is named ('copy folder + pg_dump', ADR-009) but is not a real, automated, tested procedure, and it is inconsistent: artifacts live as files on disk while metadata/state/checkpoints live in Postgres, so 'copy the project folder' alone does NOT capture a consistent backup (the DB is shared across all projects, not per-folder). A naive folder-copy + a separately-timed pg_dump can produce an artifact set and a DB snapshot that disagree (dangling path refs or missing rows). Invariant #4 ('accepted assets immutable / never lost') depends on a coherent backup story that doesn't exist.
findings.evidence: ADR-009 (DECISIONS.md:111) 'backup = copy project folder + pg_dump'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 156 same; DATA_MODEL.md invariant 4 (line 66) 'Accepted/selected assets are immutable... never lost'; the store is a single app-wide Postgres (ADR-009) not per-project, so per-folder copy is incoherent with the DB.
findings.proposedFix: Define a single 'export/backup project' operation that atomically bundles the project's artifact files PLUS a filtered DB dump (just that project's rows + its checkpoints) into one restorable archive, and a matching restore that re-points artifact paths. Document quiescence (no in-flight run during backup) or snapshot-consistency. If full per-project backup is deferred, flag it explicitly and state the interim guarantee (e.g. whole-data-dir cold copy only).

findings.finding: No update/distribution mechanism is defined for how a new build actually reaches the 'few known users', and the deferral of auto-update collides with the rollback/migration gaps above. Auto-update is deferred (§16, §18) which is a reasonable scope cut — but the deferral leaves a gap: if updates are manual (replace the .app), there is no defined trigger point for running migrations, taking the pre-migration snapshot, or performing the PG-version-compat check. 'Manual replace the app bundle' is itself an undocumented deploy procedure with the most failure surface (user double-clicks new app over an old data dir).
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §16 line 222 and §18 line 233 defer 'installers/code-signing/auto-update'; §2 line 50 'Deferred (flagged): installers/code-signing/auto-update'. No replacement manual-update procedure or migration-on-first-launch-of-new-build hook is specified.
findings.proposedFix: Even with auto-update deferred, the binding doc must define the manual-update procedure as the MVP deploy path: on first launch of a new build, (1) read data-dir version stamp, (2) check PG binary major-version compat, (3) snapshot, (4) run Alembic upgrade, (5) verify, with a clear failure/rollback path. State that this 'migrate-on-launch' hook is the seam auto-update later plugs into.

findings.finding: Blender 'detect-or-bundle' ambiguity leaks into the deploy story. §16 and ADR-006 leave Blender as 'detect-or-bundle' undecided; this materially changes the notarization signing inventory (bundling Blender = signing a large third-party GPL binary tree + a GPL source-offer obligation) and the first-run experience (detected Blender = a runtime version/availability check + failure path if absent or wrong-version). The deploy section should not stay ambiguous on this because it changes the signed bundle contents and the R4 risk surface.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §16 line 220 'Blender (detect-or-bundle, GPL source link)'; ADR-006 (DECISIONS.md:16) 'Detect/bundle'; §4 line 84 'local Blender install (detected/bundled)'. The choice is left open in three places.
findings.proposedFix: Resolve detect-vs-bundle for MVP in the binding doc (given Mac-first + pinned Blender 5.1.x, bundling gives reproducibility but adds signing/GPL weight; detecting adds a runtime version-gate + 'install Blender' onboarding step). Whichever is chosen, fold it into the §16 signing inventory and add the corresponding first-run check (version-pinned detect failure path, or bundled-Blender deep-sign).

deploy-rollback.notes:
Posture = production-grade; the handoff explicitly names deploy/rollback as a CRITICAL gap class to audit. Against that bar this dimension is materially under-built: the entire deployment story is ~6 lines in ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §16 plus scattered ADR-009/R4 mentions. The build is correctly forward-looking (no CI/.github yet — repo is still in planning), so these are architecture-spec gaps to fix in the binding ARCHITECTURE.md, not missing code.

Three critical, load-bearing gaps cluster around the shared local Postgres: (1) NO rollback/downgrade story at all (Alembic named, no downgrade()/snapshot/version-skew policy); (2) NO data-dir↔app-version compatibility stamp/gate, which is especially dangerous because the LangGraph checkpointer shares the DB, so migrations can break the reconcile-and-resume guarantee (REQ-NF-102 / Flow I) — the draft never reconciles 'migrate on update' with 'resume in-flight runs'; (3) bundled-Postgres first-run init and MAJOR-version upgrade across app updates are unaddressed (PGDATA from PG N is unreadable by PG N+1 without pg_upgrade — a silent data-loss landmine). 

R4 notarization is acknowledged as the top deploy risk but its 'verification plan' is prose ('verify on a clean machine'), missing the concrete signing inventory (4 nested binary trees: sidecar, Postgres+pgvector, Blender, Node @s4tk worker), entitlements, and the codesign --verify / spctl / stapler validate CI gates.

Recommend the human resolve, before finalize: (a) the version-skew policy (open/migrate/refuse) and downgrade support level; (b) the PG-major-upgrade strategy on app update; (c) detect-vs-bundle Blender (changes the signing surface). These are the load-bearing decisions blocking a complete §16/§7.

findings.finding: The localhost IPC boundary is protected by 'localhost-only bind' alone, with no command-origin authentication. Any local process (or a malicious web page via DNS-rebinding / a browser hitting 127.0.0.1:<port>) can issue REST commands to the sidecar — which is the SOLE WRITER of all project state and the trigger for paid cloud jobs and Mods-folder writes. 'localhost-only bind' is necessary but NOT sufficient as a trust boundary on a multi-process desktop OS; it is named as the entire control and never hardened.
findings.evidence: RISKS.md trust-boundary row 1 (line 30): control = 'schema-validate every command; sidecar = sole writer; localhost-only bind'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §15(a) (line 209) repeats 'validate all commands; sidecar is sole writer' with no auth token. §6.1 (line 124) and ADR-001 describe 'FastAPI on a dynamically-chosen free localhost port' with no per-session secret/token. RISKS.md row 1 'What can go wrong' even lists 'forged commands' but the mitigation column has no authentication, only 'versioned contract; idempotent commands'.
findings.proposedFix: Add a per-launch shared-secret/loopback token: sidecar generates a random token at startup, hands it to the Electron renderer over the already-trusted parent→child channel, and requires it on every REST/SSE/cancel request (reject otherwise). Bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1 (not 0.0.0.0), validate Origin/Host headers to block DNS-rebinding, and state this in ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1/§15 as the IPC auth control with a test (unauthenticated request from another origin is rejected).

findings.finding: Secret redaction is asserted 'everywhere' (logs/traces/DB) but there is no specified redaction mechanism, no single egress chokepoint, and no enumeration of what counts as a secret/PII. 'Redaction everywhere' with no implementation point reliably leaks: API keys land in exception stack traces, HTTP client debug logs, LangGraph checkpoint State (which carries provider inputs and is persisted to Postgres), and LangSmith spans capturing tool inputs. The trace schema (OBS-001 / DATA_MODEL Trace) explicitly stores 'inputs' and 'tool inputs', which is exactly where keys and prompts leak.
findings.evidence: RISKS.md R11 (line 20) mitigation 'redaction in logs/traces; never in DB' and boundary rows (lines 31-35) repeat 'redact keys' / 'no secrets/PII' with no named filter. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §7 (line 158) and §15(c) (line 210) say 'never in DB/logs/traces' / 'no secrets/PII in traces' but no §6 module owns redaction. PRD OBS-001 (lines 1001-1002) requires traces store 'Tool inputs' and 'Tool outputs', and DATA_MODEL Trace entity (line 30) lists 'inputs, outputs' as persisted fields — the leak surface — with no scrubber.
findings.proposedFix: Define a redaction module as a named architecture component: (1) a single secrets accessor that never returns keys into State/logs (adapters read keys at call time, never store them in LangGraph State or step inputs); (2) a structured-logging + trace pre-export filter (deny-list of key names + regex for known key formats + PII allowlist) applied at the OTel/LangSmith span processor and the logging formatter; (3) the secret-scan test (R11 'secret-scan of logs/traces/DB') promoted to a CI gate that fails the build on a hit. Anchor it in ARCHITECTURE.md §15.

findings.finding: Donor-read / Mods-write safety relies on 'never overwrite without confirm' and 'backup', but no concrete no-clobber mechanism, backup format, or rollback path is specified. The Mods folder is the user's live game install; a partial/failed export (R10 crash, R7 patch drift) writing into it can corrupt existing installed CC. There is no atomic-write (write-temp-then-rename), no namespacing/collision rule for output package filenames vs. the user's existing packages, and 'backup' is undefined (what is backed up, where, how restored).
findings.evidence: RISKS.md trust-boundary row 5 (line 34): 'read-only donors; never overwrite without confirm; path config' / mitigation 'confirm prompts; backup; isolated output'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §15(e) (line 213) repeats 'read donors, write Mods folder — never overwrite without confirm' with no mechanism. USER_FLOWS Flow F (lines 89-95) describes test-install to the Mods folder but only says 'test-install/path error → surfaced, export artifact still retained' — no clobber/backup detail. NFR §22.6 (PRD line 1510) requires 'Failed jobs must not overwrite accepted assets without confirmation' but says nothing about the external Mods folder.
findings.proposedFix: Specify in ARCHITECTURE.md §9/§15: (1) donor packages opened read-only (open with read flags; never write back to the game install dir); (2) export writes to the app's own output dir first, then test-install copies with atomic temp-write + rename and a collision check against existing filenames in Mods; (3) a defined output-namespace (e.g., app-prefixed package filenames + unique TGI instance allocation) so two runs and the user's existing CC never collide; (4) define 'backup' concretely (copy any file about to be overwritten into a timestamped backup subfolder) and surface a restore action.

findings.finding: 'Never trust provider output unvalidated' is a slogan with no defined validation contract for untrusted cloud artifacts. Provider responses are downloaded binaries (GLB meshes, DST/DDS textures, images) and JSON fed straight into Blender (bpy script), @s4tk, and DBPF embedding. The only named limit is 'validate/limit responses' (size). There is no spec for: max download size enforcement, content-type/magic-byte verification before handing bytes to Blender, decompression-bomb protection, or sanitization of provider-supplied filenames/paths (path-traversal when 'fetch(urls)→local artifacts' writes to the per-project artifact dir).
findings.evidence: RISKS.md trust-boundary row 2 (line 31): control 'validate/limit responses; never trust output unvalidated' — no concrete checks. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.4 (line 137) provider interface 'fetch(urls)→local artifacts' with no validation step; §15(b) (line 210) 'validate/limit responses' only. DATA_MODEL invariant 10 (line 75) requires 'deterministic validation before being written to project state' but that is about agent/MCP outputs and mesh QA, not raw byte/transport safety. EVAL-005 mesh QA (PRD §19.5) checks mesh plausibility but runs AFTER the bytes are already on disk and imported into Blender.
findings.proposedFix: Add a provider-output validation contract to ARCHITECTURE.md §6.4/§15: enforce a max-bytes cap on every fetch with streaming abort; verify content-type + magic bytes (GLB header, PNG/DDS signature) before persisting; sanitize provider-supplied filenames and resolve the write path under the project artifact root (reject path traversal / absolute paths); cap archive expansion. Make this a pre-Blender gate, not just downstream mesh QA.

findings.finding: LangSmith egress redaction ('artifact refs only, no PII/secrets') has no enforcement point and the threat is understated. LangSmith is hosted SaaS (ADR-007 confirms self-host is enterprise-gated and rejected) — so EVERY traced prompt, item description, style note, and tool input leaves the machine to a third party, conflicting with the local-first promise. The mitigation 'refs not binaries' addresses artifact size, not the actual data-egress risk (the user's creative prompts and any embedded secrets in span attributes still egress). 'fail-open' tracing is correct for availability but creates a silent-failure path: if the redaction filter throws, fail-open could mean the span is sent WITHOUT redaction rather than dropped.
findings.evidence: RISKS.md R6 (line 15) + trust-boundary row 3 (line 32): 'fail-open; no secrets/PII; refs not binaries'. ADR-007 (lines 84, 87) explicitly: 'SaaS data-egress (prompts/traces leave the machine)', self-host '$950+/mo → not viable'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §15(c) (line 210) 'fail-open; no secrets/PII in traces; artifact refs only'. The conflict with 'project data stays local' (ADR-007 line 84, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT line 63) is acknowledged but not reconciled with a redaction enforcement design.
findings.proposedFix: Specify the egress filter as a LangSmith/OTel span processor that runs BEFORE export and fails CLOSED on filter error (drop or scrub the span, never send raw). Define exactly which fields egress (status, timings, cost, artifact refs, redacted prompts) vs. stay local. Given the local-first conflict, state a default-private posture (e.g., a config flag to route to local Phoenix/Langfuse per the ADR-007 fallback, or send-prompts opt-in) and document that user prompts/style notes are egressed when LangSmith is enabled.

findings.finding: The deterministic-validation-before-write boundary (the core agent-safety guarantee) is stated as invariant but the validation gate is not specified for two of the highest-trust writers: the Blender bpy script and the @s4tk packager both consume LLM/agent-produced parameters and write to project state and ultimately the user's game install, yet the 'deterministic validation' that must precede those writes is never defined as a concrete schema/check. MCP-003 / ORCH-004 say agent output must pass deterministic validation, but the architecture does not name WHERE that validator lives for the Blender param graft and the tuning-clone graft (the functional overlay edits OBJD/tuning keys).
findings.evidence: PRD MCP-003 (lines 979-980) 'MCP-driven actions must still pass deterministic validation before being accepted'; ORCH-004 (lines 928-931) 'Agents must not write unstructured project state directly without validation'. DATA_MODEL invariant 10 (line 75). RISKS.md boundary row 4 (line 33) 'deterministic validation before state writes (MCP-003/ORCH-004)'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.7 (line 148) 'structured outputs validated before writing state' and §6.5 (line 142) 'validate in/out' — but no §6 module defines the validator for the tuning-graft (FunctionalOverlay donorRef/tuningKeys edits, DATA_MODEL line 21/24) or the Blender game-ready graft params. The functional overlay clones EA tuning and writes OBJD/FTPT/RIG keys — a corrupt graft here ships broken in-game content.
findings.proposedFix: Name a deterministic validation gate per untrusted-write path in ARCHITECTURE.md §6: (a) LLM structured outputs → pydantic schema validation (already implied, make it a named gate per worker in §6.7); (b) Blender game-ready params → deterministic post-conditions (scale within donor bbox, normals present, LOD count, meshgroup match) before the GEOM is accepted; (c) tuning-clone graft → validate only allow-listed TGI/tuning keys are swapped and donor preserveKeys are intact before re-serialize. Tie each to its EVAL harness so the gate is testable.

findings.finding: Subprocess command-validation for the Blender CLI worker is implied but the injection surface is not called out. The Blender worker is invoked as 'blender --background --factory-startup --python <script>' and the @s4tk worker is a Node subprocess; both receive file paths and params that originate from user prompts / provider outputs. The dimension brief lists 'command validation' for the sidecar but the artifacts only mention 'localhost-only bind + command validation' for the IPC layer, never argument/path validation for the spawned subprocesses (a provider-supplied or LLM-supplied filename flowing into a subprocess arg/Blender script).
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4 (lines 79-81), §6.5 (line 142) describe Blender/@s4tk subprocess workers with 'timeouts, structured errors, process-tree teardown' but no input-arg/path sanitization. RESEARCH R-008 (line 73) notes both CLI & bpy 'install/enable a pinned add-on per run' — another injection path. RISKS.md boundary row 4 (line 33) covers crash/hang/bad-GEOM but not arg/path injection into the subprocess invocation.
findings.proposedFix: State in ARCHITECTURE.md §6.5/§6.8 that subprocess workers receive arguments via argv arrays (never shell string interpolation), all file-path args are resolved/validated under the project artifact root, and the per-run Blender add-on is the vendored pinned one only (no dynamic script path from untrusted input). Low effort, closes the local injection gap.

security-trust.notes: Audited the RISKS.md trust-boundary table (6 boundaries) against ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6/§7/§15, the ADRs (esp. ADR-007 LangSmith SaaS, ADR-009 keychain), PRD (OBS-001 trace fields, MCP-003/ORCH-004, NFR §22.6), DATA_MODEL (Trace entity, invariant 10), USER_FLOWS Flow F, and RESEARCH R-003/006/007/008. The boundaries are all NAMED — none is entirely missing — but under the production-grade posture most are hand-waved: asserted as slogans ('redact everywhere', 'never trust output unvalidated', 'never overwrite without confirm') with no enforcement point, no testable mechanism, and no owning module in §6. The two CRITICAL items are load-bearing for a human decision: (1) the localhost IPC has authentication-by-bind only (a real forged-command / DNS-rebinding hole on a desktop OS, and RISKS.md itself lists 'forged commands' as the threat), and (2) secret redaction has no chokepoint while the trace schema explicitly persists tool inputs — the exact leak surface. The most consequential downstream-safety gaps are the undefined no-clobber/backup for the user's live Mods folder and the missing provider-output (untrusted-binary) validation contract before bytes reach Blender/@s4tk. Recommend the finalizer pin: an IPC auth token, a named redaction/egress-filter module that fails CLOSED, an atomic no-clobber Mods-write + backup spec, and a per-write-path deterministic validation gate (LLM schema / Blender post-conditions / tuning-graft key allowlist).
