findings.finding: The DIAGRAM_PLAN diagrams only ONE of the project's enumerated state machines (the 13-state item machine, sub-diagram #2). DATA_MODEL.md explicitly defines a Run/Step 8-state machine plus Project, ConceptCandidate, MeshCandidate, FunctionalOverlay, and ExportArtifact state machines. The Run/Step 8-state machine is the orchestration spine (PRD ORCH-002: pending/running/succeeded/failed/skipped/waiting-for-user/retrying/cancelled) and drives the entire job/run engine, the SSE progress stream, and the reconcile logic — yet it has no planned diagram.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL.md 'State Machines' section enumerates 6+ machines (Project; Item 13-state; Run/Step 8-state; ConceptCandidate; MeshCandidate; FunctionalOverlay; ExportArtifact). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT #sec-5 says '8-state run/step'. PRD ORCH-002 §16.3 mandates the 8 step states. DIAGRAM_PLAN.md sub-diagram #2 covers only 'Item state machine (13 states)'.
findings.proposedFix: Add a P0 'Run/Step (8-state) orchestration state machine' diagram (Mermaid state) anchored to #sec-6.2/#sec-6.3 and DATA_MODEL, showing waiting-for-user (the interrupt() gate), retrying, cancelled, and skipped transitions. Optionally fold Project/Concept/Mesh/Overlay/Export into a single 'secondary state machines' diagram so the item machine isn't the only one drawn.

findings.finding: There is no diagram for the bundled-binary supervisor / runtime lifecycle, despite it being a named production mechanic across 4 runtimes. The deployment diagram (#9) shows the static bundle TOPOLOGY (what is packaged) but not the dynamic LIFECYCLE (free-port selection -> spawn -> /health poll -> supervised restart with backoff -> process-tree teardown) that prevents orphan processes and port conflicts.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT #sec-6.8 'Supervisor' (lifecycle for Postgres, Python sidecar, Blender-detect: free-port, spawn, /health poll, supervised restart w/ backoff, clean teardown, REQ-O-103). RISKS.md R10 (orphan processes/port conflicts, Sev Med, Likelihood Med-High, 'In ARCH? Yes §6.8'). DIAGRAM_PLAN.md #9 is scoped to 'bundle + signing surface', not the runtime supervisor state machine.
findings.proposedFix: Add a P1 'Supervisor / process lifecycle' diagram (Mermaid state or flowchart) anchored to #sec-6.8 + RISKS R10, covering the start/health/restart-with-backoff/stop loop and process-tree teardown for Postgres + sidecar + Blender + @s4tk.

findings.finding: The per-node two-phase cloud submit/poll happy path (the exact mechanism that PREVENTS double-billing under LangGraph replay) is only implied inside the crash-recovery diagram (#3). R9 ('resume double-execution', Sev High) is a steady-state correctness mechanic — @task-wrap, store job_id BEFORE any side effect, durability='sync' — distinct from the reopen/reconcile flow. Drawing it only as part of crash recovery hides the normal-operation node contract that the whole reconcile spine depends on.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT #sec-6.3 'Cloud steps = two-phase nodes (@task idempotent submit -> store job_id -> poll/reconcile)'. RISKS.md R9 (High sev, 'store job_id before any side effect', durability='sync', 'In ARCH? Yes §6.2,§6.3'). DIAGRAM_PLAN.md #3 mentions '@task/idempotent-submit' but is scoped to crash recovery ('app reopen -> enumerate incomplete threads').
findings.proposedFix: Either add a small P1 'Two-phase cloud node (submit/store-job_id/poll) idempotency' sequence diagram anchored to #sec-6.3 + RISKS R9, or explicitly extend #3's 'Must show' to include the steady-state two-phase node lifecycle (not just the resume path) so the kill-after-submit/no-double-submit guarantee is visually pinned.

findings.finding: The UI-as-reconnectable-observer mechanic (SSE reconnect + Last-Event-ID replay after a UI crash while the sidecar keeps running) has no diagram. This is a load-bearing durability/availability claim of ADR-001 (sidecar survives UI crashes; UI reconnects and replays), and it is a distinct flow from server-side crash recovery (#3, which is about the sidecar/runs crashing, not the UI).
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT #sec-4 ('Survives UI crashes; UI reconnects and replays over SSE') and #sec-6.1 ('SSE ... resumable: Last-Event-ID'); DECISIONS ADR-001 'UI = thin reconnectable observer'; RISKS trust-boundary table 'reconnect+replay'. No DIAGRAM_PLAN.md entry depicts the UI disconnect->reconnect->replay sequence.
findings.proposedFix: Add a P2 sequence diagram (or a lane in sub-diagram #1) showing UI subscribe -> SSE stream -> UI crash/close -> sidecar continues run -> UI reconnect with Last-Event-ID -> event replay/catch-up, anchored to #sec-4 + #sec-6.1 + ADR-001.

findings.finding: The scoped repair loop (System Flow H / ORCH-005) is only represented as a single 'scoped-repair re-entry' edge inside the item state machine (#2). The repair-loop MECHANIC — rerun only the failed stage, preserve upstream accepted artifacts + lineage, and record the new attempt as a NEW candidate (history retained) — is a PRD-mandated behavior with no flow diagram of its own.
findings.evidence: USER_FLOWS.md 'System Flow H — Scoped Repair Loop' and PRD ORCH-005 §16.6 (regenerate concept/mesh/cleanup/overlay, exclude-and-continue). DIAGRAM_PLAN.md #2 only notes 'scoped-repair re-entry' as a state-machine edge; no dedicated repair-loop diagram, and the new-candidate/lineage-preservation aspect is not captured by a state edge.
findings.proposedFix: Add a P2 'Scoped repair loop' flowchart anchored to #sec-8/#sec-10 + USER_FLOWS Flow H, showing failed-stage isolation, new-candidate creation, upstream-lineage preservation, and exclude-and-continue, so the 'failure of one item never corrupts others' invariant is visualized.

diagrams.notes: The DIAGRAM_PLAN is largely strong on the three mechanics the prompt flagged: reconcile-resume (#3, P0), clone-a-donor export (#4, P0), trust boundaries (#6, P1), the dependency DAG (#5, P1), and the item state machine (#2, P0) are ALL covered and well-scoped. So this dimension is NOT clean, but the gaps are mostly 'important/nice-to-have' rather than critical — there is no top-tier mechanic left entirely undrawn. The most defensible gaps: (1) only the item state machine is diagrammed even though DATA_MODEL.md enumerates 6+ state machines, with the Run/Step 8-state machine being the orchestration spine; and (2) no supervisor/process-lifecycle diagram despite §6.8 + R10 (Med-High likelihood orphan-process/port risk) being explicit production concerns. The other three (two-phase node idempotency vs R9, SSE reconnect/replay, scoped repair loop) are mechanics currently folded into broader diagrams; calling them out separately would strengthen coverage but is not strictly mandatory. Only the first two are load-bearing enough to warrant a human decision before finalizing the diagram set; the rest can be resolved as 'extend an existing diagram's Must-show list' rather than net-new diagrams. No invented gaps: eval-harness map (#8), domain/lineage (#7), and deployment (#9) adequately cover their areas.

findings.finding: Hidden cross-edge collapses the two 'independent' spike-gated tracks C (Sims export) and D (Mesh/Blender GEOM) into one. §4a lists Track C (@s4tk export) and Track D (Blender game-ready GEOM) as separate 'independent parallel build tracks,' but the worker contract in §4a item 4 makes ExportJob CONSUME 'GEOM bytes' produced by BlenderJob, and ADR-005 states the 'hard split: MESH stage (→GEOM bytes, ADR-006) is separate from PACKAGE stage (s4tk embeds bytes).' Track C cannot prove its acceptance signal (a placeable .package via test-install) without Track D's GEOM output. The CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF S1 spike makes this explicit: S1 = 'prove @s4tk clone-a-donor + a headless GEOM path produces a placeable object via test-install' — i.e. S1 requires BOTH C and D simultaneously. They are not independently shippable/verifiable; they share the GEOM-bytes seam and the single highest-risk spike.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4a 'Independent parallel build tracks' lists Track C and Track D separately + worker-contract item 4 (ExportJob in: donor+GEOM+textures); ADR-005 'Hard split: MESH stage (→GEOM bytes) is separate from PACKAGE stage'; CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF S1 couples '@s4tk clone-a-donor + a headless GEOM path … via test-install'; DIAGRAM_PLAN diagram 4 (clone-a-donor) shows Blender GEOM feeding @s4tk in one flow.
findings.proposedFix: In §4a, stop labeling C and D as fully independent. Either (a) reframe the integration as 'C and D meet at the GEOM-bytes worker seam; both feed S1 and must be sequenced together for placeability verification, with mocked GEOM bytes allowing C to build packaging logic in parallel before D's real GEOM exists,' or (b) explicitly call out the GEOM-bytes contract (byte format + LOD set + meshgroup layout) as a SIXTH frozen-first contract so C can develop against a mock GEOM blob. State which.

findings.finding: Track F (Observability + evals) is declared independent but has a hard, undeclared runtime dependency on Track D (Blender). §4a Track F = 'LangSmith wiring + metric component layer,' listed as independent. But §14 and ADR-008 state the image-to-3D fidelity metric MUST render via Blender because 'headless GPU offscreen via pyrender/Open3D is broken on Apple Silicon → reuse the Blender stage as the render bridge.' So a core eval harness (the image-to-3D bakeoff fidelity scoring, EVAL-003) cannot run without the Track D Blender worker. §4a's integration-owner note ('A↔B↔(C,D,E) meet at the sidecar') omits F's edge to D entirely.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4a Track F listed as independent + integration note names only A,B,C,D,E; §14 'image-to-3D fidelity = Blender --background multi-view render … reuse the Blender stage as the render bridge'; ADR-008 item 2 same; §4 lists Blender worker as owning 'the render-bridge for evals.'
findings.proposedFix: Add an explicit F→D edge in §4a: 'Track F's mesh/image-fidelity evaluators depend on the Blender render-bridge (Track D); F can build schema/dataset/CI scaffolding and image-only metrics independently, but mesh-fidelity scoring is gated on D's render bridge.' Reflect the F→D arrow in DIAGRAM_PLAN diagram 5 (currently only shows layer import arrows).

findings.finding: Sub-section anchors referenced by downstream artifacts do not exist. The draft defines only section-level anchors #sec-1…#sec-23 (confirmed by the §22 Spec Anchor Index, which lists no sub-anchors). Yet DIAGRAM_PLAN cites '#sec-6.5' and '#sec-6 (6.2/6.3)' as bind targets, and the draft's own §6 prose uses 6.1–6.8 as logical labels with no anchor. The build contract says 'Tasks bind to the §<N> anchors here' and the handoff says 'every task bound to a #sec- anchor' — tasks pointed at #sec-6.5 (the export/worker module) will not resolve to a real anchor, and §6 bundles 8 distinct load-bearing subsystems (IPC, job engine, graph, adapters, workers, registries, LLM workers, supervisor) under one anchor, making fine-grained task binding impossible.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §22 index lists only #sec-1…#sec-23 (no sub-anchors); §6 contains 6.1–6.8 as plain text headings, not anchors; DIAGRAM_PLAN diagram 4 'Anchors: #sec-9, #sec-6.5, #sec-14' and diagram 3 'Anchors: #sec-6 (6.2/6.3)'; build-contract line 17 + handoff line 'every task bound to a #sec- anchor.'
findings.proposedFix: Either promote the load-bearing §6 subsystems to first-class anchors (e.g. #sec-6-ipc, #sec-6-engine, #sec-6-graph, #sec-6-adapters, #sec-6-workers, #sec-6-registries, #sec-6-supervisor) and add them to the §22 index, or add explicit {#sec-6.x} anchors matching the 6.1–6.8 numbering the other docs already cite. Update DIAGRAM_PLAN/ADR cross-refs to the real anchor IDs.

findings.finding: §4a omits B→D and B→C edges that the architecture actually requires, understating the sidecar/graph's coupling. §4a's import-direction rule routes everything through the sidecar, and Track B is 'Pipeline core … mock stages.' But Tracks C, D, E are the REAL implementations of stages the graph (B) invokes via the two-phase/worker contracts; B's graph nodes import the worker/provider contracts and dispatch to C/D/E. The draft says 'the sidecar is where A↔B↔(C,D,E) meet' but never states that B holds a build-time dependency on the §4a contracts that C/D/E implement, nor that B must ship mock C/D/E to be independently testable. This is implied (Track B = 'mock stages') but the dependency direction (B depends on the worker+provider contract interfaces; C/D/E depend on the same; mocks let them decouple) is not drawn — a reader could wrongly parallelize B against contracts that aren't frozen yet.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4a import rule 'Pipeline/Graph → Stages → Adapters/Workers'; Track B '(LangGraph graph … mock stages)'; §6.3 'one node/subgraph per stage'; §6.5 workers 'behind worker contracts (§4a)'; integration note names A↔B↔(C,D,E) but no explicit edge labels.
findings.proposedFix: Make the seam explicit in §4a: state that Track B builds against the FROZEN worker+provider+registry contracts using mock C/D/E stages, and that B's independence is conditional on those contracts being frozen first. Add the B→(worker/provider contract) and C/D/E→(same contract) edges so the 'frozen-first' precondition is visibly load-bearing for B's parallelism, not just A's.

findings.finding: The five frozen-first contracts are named as merge seams but their schemas are not pinned in the draft, so the parallelization claim ('after contracts freeze') has nothing concrete to freeze. §4a lists IPC contract, domain types, provider interfaces, worker contracts, registry schemas — but provider interfaces are only sketched (submit/poll/fetch signatures with no payload schema), worker contracts list in/out nouns not field-level schemas, and the GEOM-bytes format (the C↔D seam, see critical finding) is absent. The handoff explicitly defers this ('Frozen-first contracts … Brain 2 should pin these in ARCHITECTURE.md §6/§4a before tracks fan out'), confirming it is unresolved in the draft. Until pinned, Tracks A–F cannot actually fan out, so the entire multi-track parallelization seam is currently aspirational.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4a 'Frozen-first contracts (the integration seams)' items 1–5 give names/nouns not schemas; §6.4 provider iface = signatures only; §6.5 worker contracts = in/out noun lists; CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF line 'Frozen-first contracts (Brain 2 should pin these in ARCHITECTURE.md §6/§4a before tracks fan out): IPC schema, domain types, provider interfaces, worker contracts, registry schemas.'
findings.proposedFix: This is the explicit Brain-2 task: in the binding ARCHITECTURE.md, give each of the 5 (6 with GEOM-bytes) frozen-first contracts a concrete, versioned schema (pydantic/TS field-level for IPC + domain types; full method signatures + payload schemas for provider/worker interfaces; the GEOM-bytes byte/LOD/meshgroup spec). Gate the §4a 'after contracts freeze' fan-out on these being pinned. Confirm with the human which contracts are truly frozen vs. allowed to evolve.

findings.finding: Track labels are inconsistent between the draft and the PRD's own parallel-implementation plan, risking confusion in task generation. §4a defines Tracks A (UI), B (Pipeline core), C (Sims export), D (Mesh/Blender), E (Providers), F (Obs/evals). The PRD §25 defines a DIFFERENT Track A–D scheme (A: Full UI w/ mocks, B: Pipeline vertical slice, C: Connect UI to pipeline, D: Harden & evaluate). Same letters, different meanings. The draft never notes this re-mapping, so a downstream reader cross-referencing PRD §25 Track C ('connect UI to pipeline') vs draft Track C ('Sims export') will conflate them.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4a Tracks A–F; PRD §25 'Track A: Full UI with Mocked Pipeline … Track C: Connect UI to Pipeline … Track D: Harden and Evaluate.'
findings.proposedFix: In §4a add a one-line note: 'These build tracks (A–F, subsystem-oriented) supersede PRD §25's phase-oriented Track A–D scheme; do not cross-reference letters between the two.' Or rename the §4a tracks (e.g. T1–T6) to avoid the collision entirely.

anchors-dag.notes: Dimension is partially clean but has two genuine cross-edge collapses (the load-bearing finds). What's GOOD: §4a exists and is real (the template's §2.5 requirement is met) — it states an explicit import-direction rule, names 5 frozen-first contracts as integration seams, enumerates independent tracks, and explicitly states multi-track (A–F) rather than defaulting to single-track. Section-level anchors #sec-1…#sec-23 exist with a §22 index, and DIAGRAM_PLAN diagram 5 plans to draw the DAG. The two CRITICAL findings are real hidden cross-edges, not invented: (1) C (export) and D (GEOM) are labeled independent but the ExportJob worker contract consumes Blender's GEOM bytes and the S1 spike requires both at once — they collapse at the GEOM-bytes seam; (2) F (evals) is labeled independent but ADR-008/§14 force the mesh-fidelity evaluator through the Blender render-bridge (Track D) because headless GPU offscreen is broken on Apple Silicon, an undeclared F→D edge. The two most important structural gaps are the missing sub-anchors (downstream docs already cite #sec-6.5 / #sec-6.2 / #sec-6.3 that don't exist, and §6 crams 8 subsystems under one anchor) and the fact that the 'frozen-first' contracts are named but not schema-pinned, so the 'after contracts freeze' parallelization is not yet actionable (the handoff itself flags this as Brain-2's job). Recommend Brain 2: add the GEOM-bytes contract as a 6th frozen-first seam, redraw §4a edges for C↔D and F→D, promote §6 subsystems to real anchors, and pin the contract schemas before declaring tracks fan-out-ready.

findings.finding: Subprocess worker timeouts are named everywhere but never assigned a value OR a recorded deliberate deferral. §6.5 says Blender/@s4tk workers have 'timeouts, structured errors, process-tree teardown'; the trust-boundary table (RISKS.md) repeats 'timeouts' for the sidecar↔Blender/@s4tk boundary; R10 is specifically about orphan/hung processes. The Blender stage is the PRD's canonical slow-but-non-blocking hot path (LOD gen + full render + GEOM export, RESEARCH.md:45-46), and a worker hang is exactly what 'must not freeze the UI' (PRD §22.5) and R10 guard against — yet no timeout budget (or explicit 'value TBD at impl, deferred' note) exists. By contrast the team DID record a deliberate deferral for SLO numbers (PRESEARCH.md:320) and hard cost caps (PRESEARCH.md:380), so the absence here reads as an omission, not a choice.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6.5 ('timeouts, structured errors, process-tree teardown') and §6.8; RISKS.md trust-boundary row 'Sidecar ↔ Blender/@s4tk' ('timeouts'); R10. No timeout value or deferral in PRESEARCH.md §Phase-6 'NFR budgets' (lines 319-326), which only defers SLO numbers and cost ceilings.
findings.proposedFix: Add a one-line recordable item to the binding ARCHITECTURE.md (and to the worker-contract section): per-worker wall-clock timeout is a required config knob with a documented default; if a concrete number can't be set pre-spike, record it explicitly as a 'deliberate deferral — value set after S1 GEOM spike measures real Blender stage duration' so it is a tracked decision, not a silent gap. Tie hang→timeout→process-tree-kill→structured-error→retry to R10.

findings.finding: Cancel is named as a first-class capability (DELETE /jobs/{id} / WS 'cooperative cancel', PRD ORCH-006 §16.7, NFR §22.5 'cancellable/skippable') but the cancel HOT PATH has no defined semantics or responsiveness budget for the two cases that actually matter: (a) cancelling while a cloud image-to-3D job is in-flight (already submitted + possibly already billed — R9 covers double-submit but not cancel-after-submit), and (b) how fast a running Blender subprocess is actually torn down ('cooperative' implies the worker must reach a checkpoint). With no budget or behavior spec, 'cancellable where feasible' is unfalsifiable and the user-facing promise of a responsive cancel is unverifiable.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6.1 (cooperative cancel via DELETE/WS) and §11 ('cancel/skip where feasible'); PRD §16.7 ORCH-006, §22.5; USER_FLOWS.md cross-cutting + Flow C. No cancel-latency target, no statement of cloud-job cancel-vs-billed behavior, no cooperative-cancel checkpoint granularity for the Blender worker anywhere in the artifacts.
findings.proposedFix: Specify cancel semantics in ARCHITECTURE.md: (1) cloud-job cancel = stop polling + mark cancelled, with an explicit note on already-billed/abandoned outputs (reuse R8 download-on-resume logic); (2) Blender/@s4tk cancel = process-tree kill bounded by a stated max teardown window; (3) name cancel responsiveness as a recordable budget (or explicit deferral). At minimum flag as an open question for the human.

findings.finding: SSE is the single UI-responsiveness hot path (UI is a thin observer; ALL progress/log/state flows over SSE, §6.1/§11) yet there is no budget or policy on event/log volume, throttling/debounce, or the bound on the resumable replay buffer. 'Resumable: Last-Event-ID' is asserted but nothing states how long events are retained, how much is buffered while the UI is disconnected (a long Blender/cloud run could emit many log events), or whether high-frequency progress events are coalesced before hitting the renderer. Unbounded log/event streaming or an unbounded replay buffer is a real production concern (memory growth in the sidecar, UI jank) for the very subsystem the architecture leans on to keep the UI responsive.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6.1 ('SSE for progress/log/state streams (resumable: Last-Event-ID)'), §11 ('State = server-driven via SSE'); RESEARCH.md:59-60 (SSE reconnect via Last-Event-ID). No event-rate, debounce, retention-window, or replay-buffer bound stated.
findings.proposedFix: Record an SSE backpressure/retention policy line in ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1: progress events coalesced/throttled, logs streamed at info+ with a stated retention/replay window bound, and a max buffered-event count after which the UI is told to re-fetch full state. If deferred, flag it as a deliberate deferral.

findings.finding: Cold-start / reopen latency is an un-budgeted UI-responsiveness path. On every launch the supervisor does free-port selection + spawn of Postgres + Python sidecar + Blender-detect + /health polling (§6.8), and on reopen the startup reconciler enumerates incomplete LangGraph threads and re-polls in-flight cloud jobs (§6.2, System Flow I). For a local-first desktop app this startup sequence is a recurring hot path the user feels on every open, but no responsiveness expectation or deferral is recorded.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6.8 (supervisor: free-port, spawn, /health poll, restart-with-backoff) and §6.2 (startup reconciler re-polls in-flight cloud jobs); USER_FLOWS.md System Flow I; R10.
findings.proposedFix: Note startup/reconcile responsiveness as a recordable concern (e.g., async/non-blocking reconcile so the dashboard renders before reconcile completes), or explicitly defer it. No number needed — just name the path and the non-blocking requirement.

findings.finding: The soft-budget cost path is named (running estimate + warn-before-large-run, REQ-NF-103) and hard caps are correctly deferred, but the cost-ESTIMATION mechanism itself — per-op cost metadata → run rollup → pre-run estimate — is asserted without specifying where the per-op cost figures come from or that they must stay current as models/providers change. This is the data feeding a user-facing gate; if the per-adapter cost metadata is stale or missing, the warn-before-large-run promise silently degrades.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6.4 ('Cost metadata per op'), §11 ('Cost estimate surfaced; soft-budget warning'); PRESEARCH.md REQ-NF-103 + NFR-budgets (lines 308-326); DATA_MODEL.md Step/Trace carry cost?/latency? fields; A9 (PRESEARCH.md:397).
findings.proposedFix: State in §6.4 that per-adapter cost metadata is part of the provider/model registry config (so it updates with model swaps) and that the run rollup is computed from Step.cost; flag the estimation-accuracy risk as tied to A9. No dollar figures needed.

perf-budgets.notes: The perf-budgets dimension is mostly in good shape and is NOT a clean pass but close. Strengths: hot paths are explicitly named — bounded-parallel concurrency cap (~2-4, one active project; §6.2 / REQ-NF-101), two-phase async cloud nodes with job-id durability, SSE streaming for non-blocking UI, per-op cost/latency capture (Step/Trace fields), and a concrete mesh-geometry budget (~2000 tris/tile LOD0, LOD1≈30%, ~20k/item ceiling from RESEARCH.md:45). Critically, the team made the RIGHT deliberate-deferral calls and RECORDED them: PRESEARCH.md:319-326 explicitly states 'No latency/throughput SLO numbers' with rationale (PRD says no real-time; binding NFRs are responsive-UI / progress-visible / cancellable), and hard cost caps + artifact GC are flagged deferrals (PRESEARCH.md:380, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:50). So the dimension correctly avoids inventing numbers. The findings are about NAMED-BUT-UNBUDGETED-AND-UNDEFERRED concerns — places where a perf knob is asserted ('timeouts', 'cooperative cancel', 'resumable SSE') without either a value or a recorded 'value-TBD deferral', which under the production-grade posture (error paths, durability, no-UI-freeze) should at minimum be recordable deliberate deferrals. Per instructions I flagged these as open questions/absences rather than inventing thresholds. The two load-bearing items (worker timeout policy, cancel semantics) warrant a human decision before ARCHITECTURE.md is finalized because they intersect R9/R10 (double-billing, orphan processes) and the PRD's cancellable-jobs guarantee. No evidence of over-build on this dimension.

findings.finding: WHOLE CATEGORY MISSING: Onboarding / first-run. There is no first-run or setup flow anywhere. A cloud-first product (image-gen + image-to-3D + LLM all require API keys) is completely non-functional on first launch, yet the architecture never describes how a user gets from a fresh install to a working state: entering provider API keys, choosing default providers/models, locating the Sims 4 install for donors, and configuring the test-install Mods path. USER_FLOWS A–K starts at 'clicks New Project' with only a parenthetical '(optional) provider keys set'. Worse, PRESEARCH A5/R16 explicitly state the user has NO Sims 4 install yet — so the very first thing the product depends on (a game install for donors + test-install) is absent at first run, with no flow to detect/guide that.
findings.evidence: USER_FLOWS.md Flow A preconditions: 'app running; (optional) provider keys set'; ADR-009/REQ-S-101 decide WHERE keys live (keychain) but no doc gives a key-ENTRY screen or flow (grep for 'enter key/key entry/onboarding key' = 0 hits); PRESEARCH A5 'User installs Sims 4 on the Mac for the test-install loop' + R16 'No Sims 4 install yet'; PRD UI-001 Dashboard mentions 'access to settings and advanced mode' but no settings/onboarding screen is specced. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT lists 11 screens + dev panel, none of them a Settings/Onboarding surface.
findings.proposedFix: Add a first-run/onboarding subsystem + a Settings screen to §11 (and a 12th UI surface): (1) provider API-key entry writing to keychain (REQ-S-101) with per-provider validation/test-call; (2) Sims 4 install detection + manual path picker, with a graceful 'no install yet' path that disables test-install/donor-dependent stages and clearly flags it; (3) Mods-folder picker; (4) default-provider/model selection. Add a first-run state to the Project lifecycle and a User Flow 'L — First-run setup'. Mark which stages are blocked until keys/donors exist.

findings.finding: WHOLE CATEGORY MISSING: Donor library acquisition / management. 'Clone-a-donor' is the entire export strategy (ADR-005) and the #1 risk's foundation, but no subsystem, flow, or UX covers how donors are obtained, indexed, or chosen. Sims 4 does not ship individual catalog objects — it ships hundreds of large compressed full-build DBPF packages (FullBuild*.package). The app must DISCOVER, EXTRACT, and INDEX donor objects out of the user's game install, then map placement-type/archetype → a specific EA donor (DonorMapping registry), and re-validate after every EA patch (R7). None of acquisition/indexing/donor-selection/donor-caching is designed; the DonorMapping registry is described as a data file with no story for how its donorObjectKeys get populated or kept valid.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4 / ADR-005: '@s4tk ... reads donor .package from the user's game install' (single sentence, no acquisition subsystem); DATA_MODEL DonorMapping entry has 'donorObjectKey' but no producer; R7 'version-pin donor library / re-validate after patches' is a mitigation with no owning subsystem; PRESEARCH 'which EA donors to clone per archetype — research required'. There is no flow in USER_FLOWS A–K for donor discovery/selection; grep for 'donor library/donor cache/index donor' returns only the R7 risk row.
findings.proposedFix: Add a Donor Library subsystem to §6 and a system flow: (1) scan/index the user's game install (FullBuild packages) into a local donor catalog; (2) populate/validate DonorMapping registry entries against the indexed catalog; (3) a maintainer-facing donor-selection/preview UX in the dev panel; (4) post-patch re-validation job tied to R7. Sequence this BEFORE/with spike S1 — the export spike cannot run without real donors. Define what happens when a needed donor is absent (no install, wrong game version).

findings.finding: WHOLE CATEGORY UNDER-BUILT: App-update → data migration across versions. The draft covers DB schema migration (Alembic) but not the broader migration category that a long-lived, no-timebox, file+DB+registry product needs: (a) on-disk artifact-layout versioning, (b) registry-schema/registry-content versioning (PlacementType/FunctionalArchetype/DonorMapping evolve as archetypes are added), (c) LangGraph checkpoint compatibility across app upgrades (in-flight runs persisted in Postgres when the user updates the app), and (d) donor-library re-validation after an EA patch (R7) which is a data-migration event. PRESEARCH flags 'Local store schema versioning + migration' as production-hardening MUST-HANDLE, and REQ-D-101's acceptance signal is 'older project opens after schema bump' — but the architecture only names Alembic and is silent on artifact/registry/checkpoint migration.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §7 mentions only 'Alembic migrations; backup = copy folder + pg_dump'; PRESEARCH Phase-8 table: 'Local store schema versioning + migration ... production-hardening ... versioned project schema + migration path'; REQ-D-101 acceptance 'older project opens after schema bump'; R7 implies registry/donor migration after EA patches; nothing addresses LangGraph checkpoint forward-compat across app updates or artifact-layout version stamping.
findings.proposedFix: Add a Migration & Versioning section to §7/§13: stamp a schema_version on project folders + a registry_version on each registry; define a migration runner that runs on project open (DB via Alembic + on-disk artifact layout + registry content); state the policy for in-flight LangGraph checkpoints on app upgrade (drain/abandon/migrate); fold R7 donor re-validation into the same migration framework. Add a test mirroring REQ-D-101's 'older project opens after schema bump'.

findings.finding: WHOLE CATEGORY MISSING from architecture: Error taxonomy. PRESEARCH Phase-8 classifies 'Structured error taxonomy + actionable messages' as MUST-HANDLE ('error types per stage; creator vs advanced surfacing'), and PRD NFR §22.1.5 requires 'Failure messages must be actionable' with §22.3 creator-vs-advanced separation. But ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT only mentions 'structured errors' ad hoc per worker (§6.5, §15) — there is no defined error-type catalog, no creator-friendly-vs-maintainer mapping, and no contract for how errors flow over the IPC boundary to the UI. With ~10 pipeline stages, multiple cloud providers, two subprocess workers, and a translate-to-creator-language requirement, the absence of a unified error taxonomy is a real production gap.
findings.evidence: PRESEARCH Phase-8 row 'Structured error taxonomy + actionable messages | must-handle | error types per stage; creator vs advanced surfacing'; PRD §22.1.5 'Failure messages must be actionable'; PRD §10.3 / §22 require creator-friendly explanations; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT has no error-taxonomy section — only scattered 'structured error' mentions in §6.5/§15 and IPC §6.1 lists commands/SSE but no error-event schema.
findings.proposedFix: Add an Error Taxonomy section (likely under §6 contracts): a typed error enum per stage (plan/concept/mesh/blender/export/tuning/provider/system) with severity, a creator-facing message, a maintainer-facing detail/trace ref, and a retryable flag; include the error shape in the IPC SSE schema (§6.1) so the UI renders creator-vs-advanced consistently; map to ValidationResult severities where they overlap.

findings.finding: WHOLE CATEGORY MISSING: User-facing telemetry/privacy disclosure & consent. The product is branded 'local-first' yet LangSmith (hosted SaaS) receives prompts, traces, and metadata — data leaves the user's machine. This is handled ONLY as an engineering risk (R6: fail-open, redaction, refs-only) with no user-facing disclosure, consent, or opt-out. For a local-first creator tool sending the user's creative prompts to a third-party cloud, a no-consent/no-disclosure posture is a real gap (and a trust issue). There is also no opt-out path to the local-backend swap (Phoenix/Langfuse) exposed to the user.
findings.evidence: ADR-007: 'SaaS data-egress (prompts/traces leave the machine)' accepted as a design tradeoff; R6 mitigations are all internal (fail-open, redaction, artifact refs only); grep for 'privacy/consent/disclosure/opt-out' = only R6/ADR-007 engineering rows, zero user-facing consent. PRESEARCH §Phase 3 says 'No CISO / compliance / legal stakeholders' — but disclosure is a product-trust concern, not just compliance.
findings.proposedFix: Add a privacy/telemetry disclosure to onboarding/Settings: a one-line statement that prompts+traces are sent to LangSmith cloud, with an opt-out that flips the locked thin-tracing seam to the local backend (Phoenix/Langfuse) or disables external tracing entirely (fail-open already supports running without it). Record the consent state in local config. Cite this against R6/ADR-007 so the swap seam has a user trigger.

findings.finding: WHOLE CATEGORY THIN: Artifact disk-growth / cleanup is deferred without a designed seam. Multi-candidate concepts + multi-candidate meshes + multi-swatch + full-fidelity GEOM/LOD + no timebox + 'never lose accepted assets' guarantees monotonic, potentially many-GB-per-project disk growth on a local desktop. GC is explicitly deferred ('leave seams; don't build yet'), but no seam is actually specified (no retention policy hooks, no candidate-vs-accepted reclaim distinction, no disk-usage surfacing). Deferring the IMPLEMENTATION is fine; deferring the SEAM means the on-disk layout and lineage model may not support reclaiming superseded/rejected candidates later without rework.
findings.evidence: PRESEARCH Phase-8: 'Artifact storage layout + GC ... production-hardening ... retention/cleanup = deferred-but-flagged' and 'Hard cost caps, artifact GC ... leave seams; don't build yet'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18 lists 'artifact GC' under Deferred with 'seams left' but §7/§13 define no retention hook or reclaim policy; DATA_MODEL keeps superseded candidates ('history retained') with no cleanup path.
findings.proposedFix: In §7/§13, specify the GC SEAM even while deferring the implementation: tag each artifact as accepted/superseded/rejected/orphaned in the layout so a future reaper can reclaim safely; surface per-project disk usage in the UI/dev panel; document that rejected/superseded candidate artifacts are the reclaimable set. No reaper build now — just ensure the data model + layout support it.

findings.finding: WHOLE CATEGORY THIN: Multi-collection / project lifecycle management. The architecture commits to 'one active project' (concurrency) but never specifies the broader multi-project management the PRD dashboard implies: delete project, rename, duplicate/clone (valuable for re-running a theme), archive, and what 'one active project' means when a second project has an interrupted/in-flight run on reopen (reconcile-resume Flow I assumes a single run context). PRD UI-001 requires recent-projects + status, but delete/rename/duplicate and cross-project resume semantics are undefined.
findings.evidence: PRD UI-001 'Show recent projects ... project name, last modified, status'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6.2 'one active project'; USER_FLOWS Flow I (reconcile-resume) is written for a single project's runs with no statement about a second project holding in-flight cloud jobs; no flow covers delete/rename/duplicate/archive a project.
findings.proposedFix: Add project-management actions to Flow A/K and the IPC command set (§6.1): delete (with artifact cleanup + confirm), rename, duplicate-from-state, archive. Clarify reconcile-resume (Flow I) semantics across multiple projects with interrupted runs (which one resumes; what the single-writer lock means at the project level).

findings.finding: CATEGORY THIN: Undo / edit-history for creator edits. Generation history (candidates retained) and lineage are well covered, but USER-driven edits — metadata edits, include/exclude toggles, plan edits, swatch/variant selection — have no undo or revert. NFR §22.6 protects accepted assets from overwrite-without-confirm, but a non-technical creator making a mis-edit (e.g., excluding the wrong item, overwriting a name) has no undo. Lower priority than the above, but it is a whole interaction category absent for the primary (non-technical) user.
findings.evidence: USER_FLOWS Flow D 'persist edits; recompute item validation' with no undo; grep for 'undo/redo/revert/restore version' = 0 hits beyond 'generation history' (which is about generated candidates, not user edits); PRD §22.6 covers asset-overwrite confirmation only.
findings.proposedFix: Consider a lightweight undo for reversible creator edits (include/exclude, metadata, selection) — these are already persisted state changes, so an action-log + revert is cheap. Can be flagged deferred, but should be named as a known gap so the edit-persistence model leaves room for it rather than silently omitted.

completeness-critic.notes: Audited for whole MISSING CATEGORIES (not nitpicks) against the production-grade posture, reading PRD + all planning artifacts. The architecture is strong on the pipeline core (orchestration, reconcile-resume, idempotency, observability, trust boundaries, spikes-first risk sequencing) — those dimensions are well covered and I did not invent gaps there. The gaps cluster at the EDGES of the system that the pipeline-centric draft under-weighted: (1) the entire entry experience (onboarding/first-run/key entry) — critical because a cloud-first product is non-functional on first launch and the user has no Sims install yet; (2) donor library acquisition/management — a missing subsystem sitting directly under the #1 risk (clone-a-donor export); (3) app-update→data migration beyond Alembic (artifact-layout/registry/checkpoint versioning). Three CRITICAL findings are load-bearing and need a human decision before finalizing ARCHITECTURE.md: how onboarding/first-run is scoped (especially the no-Sims-install-yet path), whether a Donor Library subsystem is added now vs spike-time, and the breadth of the migration framework. The error-taxonomy and privacy-disclosure findings are important must-handle items that PRESEARCH itself flagged but the draft dropped. GC, multi-project management, and undo are thinner/deferrable but are genuine absent categories the other lenses likely skipped. Severity reflects production-grade posture: the onboarding, donor-acquisition, and migration gaps would block a real user from a successful first run or a safe app update.

citationProblems: BLEND-001 / BLEND-004 / FR-BLEND-002 / MCP-002 mandate a 3-WAY Blender spike (deterministic Python vs MCP/agentic vs hybrid) and EXPLICITLY forbid rejecting MCP prematurely ('The product must not reject MCP-driven Blender control prematurely' §15.4; 'The team must test whether Blender MCP... improves mesh cleanup' §17.2). ADR-006 contradicts these: it states 'MCP excluded' and 'MCP can't be a reproducible stage executor', demoting MCP to a manual-rescue-only tool WITHOUT running the PRD-mandated comparative spike. The architecture cites BLEND-001/EVAL-004 as covered but the spike scope has silently narrowed to Python-vs-bpy. This is a real divergence from an explicit PRD requirement that should be surfaced to the human as a scope change, not buried in an ADR.

PRESEARCH §Phase6 claims 'every in-scope requirement maps to a flow' (USER_FLOWS coverage table) and 'arch-finalize will persist the full PRD→REQ coverage table' — but neither PRESEARCH nor ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT actually contains a per-ID PRD→REQ coverage table; coverage is asserted at the category level (FR-PROJ, FR-PLAN, ...) only. Several PRD-native IDs (e.g. §10.3 unsupported-handling, the optional computer-prop archetype) thus have an ASSERTED-but-unverified citation. The finalize step (this audit) is where those gaps surface; until ARCHITECTURE.md carries the explicit table, the 'fully covered' claim in PRESEARCH P6 / USER_FLOWS is overstated.

EVAL-006 (Sims archetype mapping harness) cites fixed 'golden mappings' (CD player→electronics prop; lava lamp→light-like; etc.) but ADR-010 replaces fixed archetypes with open registries. The harness's golden-mapping pass criteria (§19.6) and EVAL-006's citation are not reconciled with the registry reframe — the architecture adopts EVAL-006 verbatim while changing the model it evaluates, leaving the eval's reference set undefined.

DIMENSION VERDICT: NOT clean — coverage is broad and the PRD-native ID adoption (PRESEARCH P6) means the vast majority of FR-/AC-/UI-/PIPE-/ORCH-/OBS-/EVAL- items are self-covering and well-mapped to ARCH anchors, DATA_MODEL entities, and USER_FLOWS. But there are 3 genuine UNCOVERED must-haves and 3 citation/consistency problems worth escalating.

HIGHEST-PRIORITY FINDINGS:
1. MCP Blender spike contradiction (citationProblem #1): ADR-006 unilaterally excludes MCP, directly violating the PRD's explicit §15.4 BLEND-004 'do not reject MCP prematurely' and §17.2 MCP-002 'must test Blender MCP'. The PRD makes the 3-way spike a hard requirement; the architecture silently reduces it to a 2-way (Python vs bpy). This is the single most defensible 'PRD requirement dropped' finding. It may be a reasonable engineering call, but per production posture it must be an EXPLICIT, human-confirmed scope change, not an ADR assertion.
2. §10.3 unsupported-generation handling is genuinely UNCOVERED as a concrete requirement — no REQ id, no module, no invariant. The open-registry reframe (ADR-010) makes 'any prop' generable, which actually INCREASES the need to define what happens when a placement type / functional archetype has no donor mapping (the real 'unsupported' case now). This is a must ('the system must either convert... or mark unsupported').
3. ORCH-003 worker-role enumeration is only ~partially satisfied by name (Product Orchestrator, Texture/Swatch worker, Human Review Gate not listed as first-class workers in ARCH §6).

SCOPE-ELEVATIONS (correctly handled, noted for completeness): test-install §8.2-should→must (REQ-O-101); AC-015 decorative export→real-placeable for ALL items (REQ-F-101); AC-013 single functional→extensible registry (REQ-F-102); multi-swatch added (REQ-F-104). These are over-build vs the literal MVP yardstick but are deliberate, user-confirmed scope decisions under the agreed production-grade-narrow-but-open posture, so NOT flagged as overbuild.

PARTIAL/RECONCILE items (covered but with an inconsistency to fix in finalization): EVAL-006 golden mappings vs open registry; the §9.1 seven decorative categories now subsumed by an open PlacementType registry (decorative breadth ok, but the 7 named categories are no longer individually guaranteed donor mappings — finalize should confirm each of the 7 has a seed PlacementType+donor so the anchor Y2K set is buildable); ORCH-006 'pause' verb is never explicitly designed (cancel+skip are).
